| 2. Sun Temple Guardian in a boat at "Mach 7", 20 ft launch, Golden Idol the best treasure | Leaps into a tiny stone speedboat (250 cruise, 360 surge); 9 s cooldown launch; Idol 17 gold | Implemented and tested |
| 3. Jet Set Radio-inspired one-button boat tricks | R (gamepad R1) in the air; combos; A/D roll, S backflip; callouts | Implemented and tested (real keys) |
| 4. Pursuers follow almost to the Hoard | No timer or leash; ends at the sanctuary | Implemented and tested (all islands, one run each or more) |
| 5. Crystal Echo small, fast, mobile | Tiny crystal rider, 230 to 340 studs/s, turns at 9 rad/s, darts | Implemented and tested |
| 6. Danger follows until near home | The sanctuary: gold lantern buoys 450 studs round the Hoard | Implemented and tested |
| 7. No horizon text | Island names, treasure tags, landmarks are short-range labels; the aim view names only its target | Implemented and tested (screenshot) |
| 8. Minimap | Top right, turns with the camera; islands, Hoard, sanctuary, tornadoes, your pursuers | Implemented and tested (screenshots) |

## 3. The six-minute round

`Config.RAID_DURATION` is 360 and the clock **does not run during deployment**. A raid opens with a 20 s launch window (V8: 40 s, with the clock running); the six-minute clock starts when it closes, so a goblin who fires late still gets all six minutes and one who fires at once gets a head start. The HUD shows `LAUNCH WINDOW 18 | RAID 6:00 STARTS AFTER`, then `RAID 5:59`. During the 10 s intermission (V8: 12) a goblin can climb into a cannon and aim; it fires from the bell (2 s after the raid starts). Measured: 367 s left on the clock with 7 s of the window to go (360 + 7).

Everything else that a six-minute raid touches:

| What | V8 | V9 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Final rush (25% more for banking) | last 90 s | last 50 s (the HUD timer says FINAL RUSH) |
| Last call (red timer) | last 60 s | last 30 s |
| Treasure interest step | 80 s | 45 s (three steps, as before) |
| Respawn of the three nearest treasures | 150 to 160 s | 100 to 105 s |
| Respawn of the rest | 60 to 70 s | unchanged |
| First storm | 50 s | 40 s; gap 35 to 60 s (V8: 45 to 75) |
| First tornado | (none) | 25 s |
| Same island's pursuer again | 40 s | 25 s |
| Shinies per raid | participation 10, gold cap 30, win 25, underdog 5, cap 70, present 90 s | 6, 22, 15, 3, 42, 60 s (about the same per hour) |

Measured with a 70 s test raid on the client HUD, second by second: the launch window counted 20 to 1, the clock started at 1:09, `FINAL RUSH` and its banner came at 0:50, `LAST CALL` and its banner at 0:30, `RAID OVER!` at 0:00, `NEXT RAID IN 10`, and the next raid opened with a new launch window. Intermission aiming, measured: a goblin climbed into a cannon 9.7 s before the bell, a fire before the bell was refused (still loaded), the raid's start did not tip them out, and the fire after the bell launched them. Respawns and late joiners were not changed (a late joiner lands on the skyship while the window is open, at home after).

## 4. The pursuit architecture

`server/Pursuit.lua` was rewritten around one idea from the playtest: **danger stays close, consequences stay small.**

- **No timer, no leash, no global cap of five.** A pursuit ends at the sanctuary, when the treasure is banked or leaves the thief's hands (it changes quarry if a rival snatches it at sea), when the thief dies or leaves, after 12 s ashore, after two explosions, at the raid's reset, or after 150 s as a backstop for one stuck behind an island.
- **Pacing from the gap, with momentum.** Far behind (over 320 studs) a pursuer surges at its form's top speed. Closing, it gains a form-specific margin on the thief's own speed. Close, it **hangs just behind** at its `follow` distance, matching speed. It speeds up and slows down at its own rates, so a thief who keeps their speed is shadowed and one who loses it (a rock, a missed hoop, a rival, a landing) is caught. Every so often it **lunges**, and that is when its tell shows.
- **Tells lock on.** During a short-range form's wind-up it holds onto the hull and matches its speed, so the strike lands unless the thief does something about it (boost, turn, jump). Bramble, who charges from 105 studs, keeps pace and lines up instead.
- **Resurfacing.** A pursuer hopelessly far behind (900+ studs, behind the thief) or blocked by land for 3 s reappears 420 studs behind the thief along their wake, never in front and never in view of their bow.
- **Pursuers fly.** `Pursuit.air` gives every kinematic pursuer an altitude: a ramp throws it, a tornado lifts and spins it, and one in the air cannot strike.
- **One thing at a time.** `Pursuit.hit` asks `Impact.open` before it touches a goblin *or their boat*, so nothing in the world juggles a goblin inside the 1.2 s grace; after the Guardian's launch nothing from the world lands for 3 s (`Impact.protect`). Hulls are never taken below 12% by a creature. The two-strike grip is unchanged.
- **Budgets.** One pursuer per island, at most two island pursuers per goblin, 14 in the whole sea; no rigid cap cancels an important chase.

## 5. Chase limits and the Hoard sanctuary

The sanctuary is the water within 450 studs of the Hoard: just off Goblin Cove's coast all round, taking in the harbor mouth (the harbor jump is 326 out) and the docks (about 210). It is marked by 24 gold lantern buoys (28 positions round the ring; the other four fall on land), a gold ring on the map and on the minimap. A pursuer never steps into it; when its thief enters, it stops at the edge, says so in its own words ("The Guardian's boat skids to a stop at the cove lights. It shakes a stone fist at you."), and sinks away. The Leviathan turns back at the lights; the Ghost Fleet wails and fades. PvP is not affected: a rival can still catch you inside.

520 studs was tried first and measured: the Coral Atoll's shore was inside it, so its clam only set out after the boat had already left the ring. At 450 the near islands' shores are outside it; their chases are short because the islands are near.

**The Watcher's rule at sea, measured:** with the boat stopped and facing away, it approached at 99 studs/s (259 to 177 studs); the boat was turned to face it and it **froze dead** (177 studs for 1.5 s, eyes dark); turned away again, it came on (146, 109, 71, 42) and began its tell at 21.

## 8. The Leviathan

**Removed:** the V8 breach (a ring on the water, then the head up through it, 48 hull) is gone from the code; nothing else imitates it. It still rises out of the water now and then for the look of it, only when it is more than 140 studs from its quarry, with a splash and no hit.

**What it does now:** it hunts as before (fast boats near the Sleeper's eye, or the Tooth's thief at sea) but **shadows**: its snout 46 studs behind the stern, matching the boat's speed, surging at 300 when far behind (a boost is 202, a full chain 242). It speeds up at 150 and slows at only 55 studs/s/s. A boat that keeps its speed is never closed below 26 studs; every 7 s it roars and lunges (a toast says "Don't slow down!"), and the lunge falls short. A boat that slows (under 80 studs/s, or 22% under its recent speed) is **caught**: bumped on (push 70, lift 42), swiped aside (82 sideways) or, if nearly stopped, tossed over its head (lift 95). A catch is a world hit (grace, grip rule, 8 hull, never sunk), and the same boat cannot be caught again for 4 s: it swerves off alongside and falls in behind. Boats beside its head are still shoved aside by its bow wave. It cannot follow into water shallower than 7 studs (it waits; after 10 s it gives up), and it stops at the sanctuary.

**Measured** (Leviathan's Rest to home, about 3,000 studs):
- Boosting the whole way: it surged from 505 to 52 studs in 4 s, then held **41 to 44 studs** behind for the whole run; lunges reached 22 to 25; **no contact**. At the end the reef outside Home Bay was too shallow for it.
- Braking hard for 2.5 s at t = 8 s: caught at 8.6 s (8 hull, grip slipped, the boat thrown up 19 to 23 studs). The first version then swam straight through the nearly stopped boat and overshot ahead; now it swerves off (gap 60 to 112) and is back on the tail at 24 studs by 16 s.
- Its blast reaction (three explosions send it home) is unchanged from V8 and was not re-run.

## 9. The Sun Temple Guardian's boat

When the Golden Idol's thief is on the water 70 studs off the temple's shore, a tiny stone speedboat (gold trim, a flaming outboard, a windshield) appears off the shore on their side, and the Guardian **leaps from wherever it stands** onto it in a high arc (1.6 s; `Threats.guardianBoard`). While it is at sea its island stands empty (`GuardianState` = `sail`), and when the chase ends it is back at its altar. The boat cruises at 250, surges at 360 ("Mach 7"), turns wide (1.9 rad/s: a hard turn makes it overshoot) and hangs 40 studs behind. **The launch:** every 9 s, within 120 studs, it raises its fists (a second pair of arms appears overhead), a 20-stud gold ring opens where the thief is going (0.85 s), and a stone fist punches up out of the sea: whatever is on the ring is thrown 118 studs/s up and 30 along its way. No grip hit, about 1 health, 4 hull, and nothing from the world lands for 3 s afterwards. A miss lets it try again in 4.5 s.

![The Guardian in its speedboat, right behind the thief](2026-10-14-v9-guardian-boat.jpg)

**Measured:** boosting home: boarded in 1.6 s, surged to 259, followed at 153 average (19 closest), two launches dodged by the boost, quit at the sanctuary edge (511), Guardian back at its altar. Cruising: the launch landed; the boat went **34 studs up** (the "20 feet", tuned for a goblin-sized world), hull 160 to 156, treasure kept, no grip slip; quit at 515. A goblin hit on foot (swimming) was not measured.

**Golden Idol:** 17 gold (V8: 11), the highest base value; every other treasure is still 4 to 11. Interest (three steps of 12%, 2 each) takes it to 23. The HUD read "YOU HAVE THE GOLDEN IDOL (17g)". The final rush (25%) applies as to anything banked.

## 10. The Golden Idol's new value

Section 9. No other value changed.

## 11. The Crystal Echo

A tiny crystal imp on a sliver of crystal (2 by 0.8 by 5.4 studs) with a trail. Speed 230, surge 340, accelerates at 480 and stops at 380 studs/s/s, turns at 9 rad/s (a skiff manages about 2.5). Far off it cuts straight at you; within 110 studs it **repeats your wake** 0.6 s behind (closing to 0.3), taking every turn you took; every 0.9 to 1.7 s it **darts**, skipping across the water straight at you. Its hit is small: thrown sideways (46), a quarter of your speed taken, 2 hull, never the treasure. It waits 2.5 s after appearing before it can strike. Tell 0.45 s, rest 3.5 s. Measured in section 7. Its first V9 version followed a point 1.4 s back along the wake, which at 180 studs/s was 250 studs behind the boat, and never struck; a frame-by-frame probe then showed its wind-up flew it straight through the boat (section 22).

## 12. The Ghost Fleet

`server/GhostFleet.lua`. Taking the Skull Chalice raises the fog and **three ghost ships** (translucent teal hulls, two masts with ragged glowing sails, a skull flag, lanterns), each with **four ghost pirates** on deck (glowing body, tricorn hat, green eyes, a cutlass) who sway and wave their cutlasses. The ships sail spread across the thief's wake (two either side, one further back, never a rigid line) at up to 170 (surge 230) and fire marked volleys of two. **Volleys throw and batter; they never loosen a grip.** Once the thief is 650 studs off Skull Rock's shore, **pirates leap from the decks** (you see them fly over in an arc) into **five tiny rowing boats** that chase at up to 290, spread across the wake; the ships fall back and sink into the fog 14 s later. A dinghy that gets within 20 studs waves its cutlass (0.7 s) and its pirate leaps aboard (a grip hit). Only one pirate leaps at a time, fleet-wide, at most every 6.7 s: longer than the grip's 6 s window, so **pirates alone can never strip a thief**. A keg or a cannonball sinks a dinghy outright. The fleet ends at the sanctuary, when the Chalice is banked or lost (it follows a new holder at sea), or at the reset. The Captain's Shade rule is unchanged: steal while his eyes are dark and the fleet rises 18 s late.

![Ghost pirates in their dinghies closing on the thief; the minimap shows four red pips](2026-10-14-v9-ghost-dinghies-minimap.jpg)

**Measured:** in the first run a volley loosened the grip and a pirate's leap 3.8 s later took the Chalice, 9 s into the escape: too harsh. Volleys lost their grip effect and the leap gap went to 6.7 s. Then: ships rose and chased (170 to 230), the dinghies went over at 5 s (crews went from 4 to 2, 2 and 3), the ships sank by 23 s, two dinghies were sunk by other blasts (the Navy was out at FRENZY heat), and the rest chased to the sanctuary (34 s). Pirates boarded every 7 to 8 s: four grip slips, **no drop**. With the Shade dozing, the fleet rose at 18 s. **Not captured:** a clear still of the ships and their crews (the Skull Rock fog and a passing tempest washed them out in the one attempt).

## 13. Boat tricks: controls and animations

**R** (gamepad **R1**) in the driver's seat while the boat is in the air (at least 5 studs up). One button, nothing to learn:

| Press | Trick | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First in a flight | SPIN CYCLE: a flat 360 | 0.45 s |
| Second | CORKSCREW: a spin and a roll at once | 0.7 s |
| Third | BOW FLIP | 0.6 s |
| Fourth | DOUBLE SPIN | 0.7 s |
| Holding A or D | PORT / STARBOARD ROLL | 0.5 s |
| Holding S | KEEL FLIP (a backflip) | 0.6 s |

A press during a trick is kept and plays the moment it ends, so mashing R strings a combo. W is ignored (a driver nearly always holds it: the first version used W to pick a front flip and every trick came out as one). On the water R only says how ("Tricks are for the air..."). The driver no longer gets the anchor's R prompt; passengers still do.

**How a trick moves the boat:** while a trick runs, `BoatSim` writes the hull's orientation outright from its heading at the start and the trick's progress (eased), and zeroes its spin; position and velocity stay physics. A trick always ends exactly level, facing the way it started. **Landings:** clean after tricks pays a speed burst (16 + 9 per trick, up to four) and hands back 0.8 s of boost cooldown per trick (the server only pays a hull it saw high in the air, once per flight); a hull still mid-trick when it touches water comes down **level anyway** ("SKETCHY!", no burst, never a capsized boat). Other players see the boat spin (the hull is replicated) and a short-range label over it ("CORKSCREW!"). Callouts are in `client/Tricks.lua`.

**Measured:** off a ramp (server physics): a spin turned the hull a full 360 in 0.55 s (V9's first timing) and ended level, facing the same way; a roll still running at touchdown snapped level (no capsize, 137 studs/s kept). **Real keys** on the client: `W`, `Shift`, `Space`, `R`: a 31-stud super jump and a corkscrew that was still running at touchdown ("SKETCHY!", landed level at full speed), which is what led to the remapping above. **Real keys** in a tornado: `R` mashed near the top chained SPIN CYCLE, CORKSCREW (x2), BOW FLIP (x3), DOUBLE SPIN (x4); the last was still running at splashdown (SKETCHY!), the boat landed upright. A clean landing after one trick from a hop showed "CLEAN! + SPEED + BOOST (x1)". **Not measured:** the boost cooldown refund itself, the gamepad button, how tricks look from a second client.

## 14. How Jet Set Radio inspired the tricks

Not its art, names, music or animations: its **attitude**. In Jet Set Radio tricks are part of ordinary travel, cheap to start, and the game shouts them at you. So: one button, tricks during any airtime (a hop, a ramp, a launch, a tornado), a combo that grows as long as you stay up, and chunky, tilted, loud callouts in shifting colour that pop in, wobble and fly off, with a landing grade (CLEAN, SMOOTH, FRESH, OUTRAGEOUS, or SKETCHY). The reward is style and a little momentum, never gold.

## 15. Ocean ramps

Seven new ramps (12 kicker ramps in the sea now), each **beside** a lane (never on its line, so a hoop chain is never thrown off), pointing the way home, on the routes away from the worst pursuers: CHIMNEY JUMP (from Crystal Isle), MILL JUMP (from Windmill Hills), EMBER ROAD JUMP (the longest open lane), FROST ROAD JUMP, TANGLE JUMP, LEVIATHAN LEAP (from Leviathan's Rest) and SKULL RUN JUMP (south-west of Skull Rock). Every ramp is checked at build time for open water to ride up and to land in (none was refused). A ramp now throws higher the faster you hit it: 76 studs/s up at 34, plus 0.2 per stud/s faster, up to 112 (about 30 studs up and 2 s in the air at boost speed), and it throws the boat **level**.

**Measured** (Mill Jump, autopilot at 177 to 190): the first version flipped the boat over backwards (upright 1.0 to -0.68 in the air) and it landed capsized, losing 110 studs/s; the plank's push was spinning it. Now the kick clears pitch and roll spin: 30 studs up, 1.1 s in the air, level throughout, landing kept the speed (146 to 159 with the landing burst). The other six ramps were placed and checked by the build, not driven.

## 16. Tornadoes: mechanics and locations

`shared/Twister.lua` (the maths, shared), `server/Tornadoes.lua` (where they are), `client/Twisters.lua` (how they look). Up to three at once, **independent of the storms** (storms keep their own spouts), the first 25 s into a raid, each lasting 70 to 105 s and wandering at 8 to 16 studs/s round one of eight open-water alleys (the West Run, the Eastern Reach, the Open Sea, the Leviathan Road, the Far North, the Cinders, Navy Waters, the Maelstrom Reach), never within 1,100 studs of the Hoard, turning away from shallow water. Half of them form at the alley nearest a goblin who is out at sea. The feed announces each one.

**The funnel:** 30 studs wide at the water, 51 at the top, 190 tall. Inside it whatever came in is caught (its motion across turned into the swirl within a fraction of a second), lifted toward a steady 74 studs/s, swung round at 58 and held toward the middle; just outside, it is drawn in and lifted a little; at the top it is thrown out. Boats are lifted by whoever simulates them (the driver's client, or the server), using the same function, so every machine agrees; the anti-cheat allows the height (300) and the speed near a tornado and for 7 s after. **The jump key bails out**: the boat is thrown 120 studs/s the way it points. A goblin on foot or swimming is thrown into the **skydive** (`Flight.launch`, 112 up), so glide, dive and the water skips all work, and falling back in throws them again. Pursuers are lifted and spun (`Pursuit.air`) and cannot strike while up there. Patrol ships are physics boats and should be lifted the same way (not tested). Sea mobs and loose treasure are not lifted.

**Measured:**
- A boat at 181 studs/s (server physics): caught, up to **198 studs** in about 3 s, thrown out, landed upright and sailed on. The first version (a weaker pull) let a boat at 110 punch straight through with a 27-stud hop.
- A client-driven boat with **real keys** at 75 studs/s: caught, up to 198, thrown out; the server saw 199 and never took the hull back.
- A goblin swimming into one: thrown 91 studs up into the skydive (tumbling), then skipped off the sea at 71 and 34.
- Bramble started inside one: lifted to 204 studs, spun, dropped back into the chase and struck shortly after landing.

## 17. Boost hoop detection

V8 asked whether the hull's **middle** was within the hoop's radius on the frame it was checked. V9 sweeps the hull from where it was at the last check to where it is now: a hoop counts if that path crosses the hoop's plane within its radius plus half the hull's width (plus 2), or if the hull ends a frame with its own length across the plane; height counts on its own, smaller reach (half the hull's height), so a boat that jumps through a hoop gets it and one that clears it does not. Chains, ceilings, cooldowns, timed courses and direction are unchanged.

Measured with a synthetic test (a skiff-sized hull moved past a radius-12 hoop, ten phases each):

| Off the hoop's middle | V8, 60 fps (4 studs a frame) | V8, 10 fps (24 a frame) | V9, either |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 to 6 studs | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 10 | 10/10 | 6/10 | 10/10 |
| 12 | 10/10 | 4/10 | 10/10 |
| 14 to 18 (hull visibly over the ring) | 0/10 | 0/10 | **10/10** |
| 19 and more (clear of it) | 0/10 | 0/10 | 0/10 |

Airborne through the middle: counted at 10, 16 and 20 studs up (the ring is 5 plus or minus 12); not counted at 22 or 26. **Not driven by hand.**

## 18. Horizon UI

![The view from a boat in open water: islands and landmarks, no names on the horizon](2026-10-14-v9-clear-horizon.jpg)

Island names show within 240 studs of the island's middle (V8: 1,500, so every island was named across the sea), treasure tags within 170 (V8: 3,000 and always on top), sea landmarks, currents, lanes, timed courses and ramps within 180 to 220 (V8: 300 to 700). The Guardian's tag shows within 120. The label over the Hoard shows only while you carry treasure, and the screen-edge arrow toward it hides while the Hoard is on screen (one marker at a time). Aiming from the skyship, only the island under the ring wears its name and tier (V8: all sixteen); the aim banner names it too. Light pillars, the Hoard's beam and prompts are unchanged. **Checked:** the open sea and a chase (screenshots); the harbor, the Hoard and the skyship aim were not each photographed.

## 19. The minimap

`client/Minimap.lua`, top right (the treasure board moved below it). A rounded square about 1,100 studs from the middle to the edge, **turning with the camera** (up is where you look), with N on its rim. It shows the islands (from the shared island list, so it cannot disagree with the world; sized to scale), the name and tier of the island you are at underneath (where island names went when they left the horizon), the Hoard and the sanctuary's ring (off the map, the Hoard is an arrow on the rim, gold and pulsing while you carry), treasure waiting or loose nearby, tornadoes, and **only what is chasing you** (a red pip; on the rim if it is off the map). It hides high in the air (the skyship, a flight). The full map (M) gained the sanctuary ring and the tornadoes.

The first version was round, using a `CanvasGroup` to clip; in Studio it did not clip at all and big islands spilled past the rim. It is now a rounded square clipped by an ordinary frame. **Checked:** screenshots in open water, at home (it named GOBLIN COVE) and in the Ghost Fleet chase (four red pips). Not checked on a small screen.

## 20. Performance

Server, one client, Studio on the development PC (not a phone, not a live server):

| Scene | Server frame rate | Heartbeat work (Stats) | Parts in Threats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A tornado, nothing chasing | 60.2 | 1.03 ms | 320 |
| Three island pursuers, a Leviathan hunt, three tornadoes | 60.2 | 1.12 ms | 342 |
| The Ghost Fleet (3 ships, 4 dinghies), two tornadoes | 60.3 | 1.26 ms | 458 |

The client held 60 frames a second. World build 5.2 to 6.2 s, sea grid 4.1 to 4.8 s (V8: 3 to 4 s and 3 s). Tornadoes cost the server a few dozen numbers (the funnels are drawn by each client: 26 parts each). A pursuer is one CFrame write a frame; the fleet poses its crew with one `BulkMoveTo`. **Not established:** anything about 32 players, a busy server, replication cost, or any phone.

## 21. Tests actually performed

All in Roblox Studio play mode on one client through the built-in Studio MCP, with a temporary test script in Workspace (never committed) that called the game's own modules, and an autopilot driving with the game's boat physics. Real key input where marked.

- **Round:** a full 70 s test raid on the client HUD (window, clock, final rush, last call, end, intermission, next raid); intermission aiming and the bell.
- **Pursuit:** every island's sea form at least once from a real theft (section 7), several twice; the Guardian four times, the Leviathan three, the Ghost Fleet four, the Echo five; the Watcher's freeze; a pursuer lifted by a tornado; a pursuer thrown by a ramp (Bramble, unplanned).
- **Boats:** a ramp before and after the fix; tricks on a ramp (autopilot) and with real keys (a super jump; a tornado combo).
- **Tornadoes:** boat (autopilot and real keys), goblin, pursuer; the anti-cheat's view.
- **Hoops:** the synthetic sweep (section 17).
- **Pictures:** tornado, Guardian boat, dinghies and minimap, horizon.
- **Checks:** StyLua, Selene and the Rojo build clean; `scripts/check.ps1` result in the pull request.

**Not performed:** anything with a second client; a human playing; a full six-minute raid start to finish with the real duration; a goblin hit by the Guardian on foot; a patrol ship in a tornado; gamepad or touch; the island bodies' fit after scaling; every ramp driven; the hoops driven by hand.

## 22. Bugs found and fixed

1. **Bramble's charge sped up every frame** (it reached 513 studs/s): the charge speed is now fixed when the charge begins.
2. **Ramps flipped boats over backwards** at V9's stronger kick (section 15).
3. **A fast tornado crossing** punched straight through the funnel (section 16).
4. **The Echo never struck:** it followed a point 250 studs back, then flew straight through the boat during its wind-up (a frame-by-frame probe showed it 28 studs past when the strike came). Tells now lock on.
5. **The Leviathan swam through a stopped boat** after a catch and overshot ahead (section 8).
6. **The Ghost Fleet stripped a thief in 9 s** with a volley plus a leap (section 12).
7. **The Coral Atoll was inside the sanctuary** (section 5).
8. **W picked the trick** (section 13).
9. **The minimap did not clip** (section 19).
10. The Guardian's state attribute said "board" while it sailed (cosmetic).
11. The launch-window timer said "6:00" whatever the raid's length.
12. Mine, in testing: my autopilot first steered at the waypoint after next and drove a skiff across the Crossroads; one tornado test was spoiled by puffer fish knocking the test boat off its line; one test teleported a goblin who was mid-skydive into a boat and it ended badly. None was the game's fault; each run was redone.

## 23. Known limitations

- **Nobody has played this and it has never had two players.** That applies to everything above.
- The Guardian leaves its island while it chases at sea: a second goblin on the Sun Temple meanwhile meets no Guardian.
- The imps can take a cruising thief's treasure with two leaps, on purpose (they are thieves); the treasure floats and can be grabbed back.
- Pursuers are kinematic: they do not collide with boats or each other; every touch is a scripted hit.
- The Watcher's "facing" is where a goblin's body (or boat) points, not their camera.
- The near islands' chases are short because the sanctuary is near them.
- Ghost ships in fog are hard to see in a still; the Leviathan's head was out of frame in the only shot of it.
- Island guardian bodies were scaled without checking how they now sit in their terrain.
- Tricks: keyboard and gamepad only; no touch button.
- A modified client driving a boat gains more room near a tornado (the anti-cheat allows 300 studs up and more speed there).
- 32-player scalability is not established.

## 24. Deferred or incomplete

Nothing of the fifteen points was left out. Incomplete: multiplayer testing; a human playtest; tornadoes lifting loose treasure or sea mobs (not attempted: pursuers and boats only); pictures of the island guardians at their new size.

## 25. Human playtest instructions

Double-click **Play Loot Goblins**, wait for Studio, press the blue Play button, press `H` for the help panel. Then try these and say what felt bad:

1. **Six minutes.** Watch the top of the screen: a launch window, then the clock. Is six minutes enough to make two or three runs?
2. **The Golden Idol** (Sun Temple). Take it, get in a boat, sail for home. Something is coming. When the gold ring opens under you, turn or boost.
3. **The Leviathan.** Take the Leviathan Tooth (far north-west) and sail home. Keep your speed up. Then try braking.
4. **The Echo** (Crystal Isle). Take the Crystal Heart and look behind you.
5. **Skull Rock.** Take the Skull Chalice and keep going. Watch the ships. Then watch behind you again.
6. **Tricks.** Hold `Shift` for a boost, press `Space` to jump, press `R` in the air. Press it again. Hold A or D and press it.
7. **A tornado.** The feed says when one forms; the minimap shows `@`. Drive into it. Press `R` near the top. Or press `Space` to bail out.
8. **The minimap** (top right): can you find your way home with it?
9. **Hoops.** Do they count when you clip one?
10. **The horizon.** Is it clearer? Is anything you needed missing?

The team's questions to answer after playing: Are the chases funnier? Does the danger stay close without feeling unfair? Is the Guardian's boat absurd enough? Do the tricks feel stylish? Is anything frustrating now? Send a screenshot of any red error.

## 26. Recommended next steps

1. **Play it with three people.** Every number above is a guess at fun until then; especially how often pursuers strike, the Echo's bump rate, and whether the imps should be able to rob you.
2. Tune the Leviathan's following distance (46) and lunge with people watching: "breathing down your neck" is a feel, not a number.
3. Look at the island guardians at their new size in their islands, and fix any clipping.
4. Give the ghost ships more presence in fog (brighter outlines or lanterns).
5. Decide whether loose treasure and sea mobs should ride tornadoes too.
6. Measure a busy server (several thieves, several chases, three tornadoes) with real clients before calling it 32-ready.

## Report: 2026-10-13-v8-chaos-and-counterplay.md

# V8: Chaos & Counterplay (2026-10-13)

Requested by Ninety with the "V8 One-Shot: Chaos & Counterplay" prompt and three sentences of his own: make me impressed, make me want to show someone, make it work reliably. Built by Claude Opus 5.5 in one session.

**Read this first.** Everything below was built and tested by one AI on **one** Roblox Studio client. Nobody has played V8, and it has never had a second player in it. "Tested" in this report means I ran it in Studio play mode and measured it, usually from the server, often with real key presses on the one client. It does not mean it is fun. Where I only have numbers and never looked at the thing, I say so.

![A goblin tumbling off the skyship over the named islands](2026-10-13-v8-tumble.jpg)

## 1. Summary of completed features

| Requested | What was built | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Freely aimable skyship cannons | Aim by looking (mouse or keys); the ring is where you land; the server works out the throw | Implemented and tested |
| Destination visibility | The ship is hidden while aiming; every major island wears its name and tier; a ring and skip marks on the water | Implemented and tested |
| Walkable wings | Gates in the rails, two wings with walkways and diving boards | Implemented and tested |
| Floppy limbs while skydiving | Limb joints switched off on the server while tumbling, back on when gliding or diving | Implemented and tested on one client; **other players' view not tested** |
| Three diminishing water bounces | 95, 66, 40 studs/s up; then a swim | Implemented and tested |
| Nerfed glide | Glide is an air brake (under 1 stud across per stud down; V7 was 5.7) | Implemented and tested |
| Catapults on the same system | All three are launchers: same aim, same flight, same landings | Implemented and tested |
| Stronger boat jump, speed-based super jump | Hop 18 studs; super jump 38 studs at 188 studs/s | Implemented and tested (real driver) |
| Every island creature pursues into the sea | 12 new sea forms on one framework, plus the Leviathan and the existing Ghost Fleet | Implemented and tested (each one run once; see section 10) |
| Creatures using boats | Bramble in a washtub, the imps' raft, the garrison's launch | Implemented and tested |
| Threat severity redesign | Grace, smaller damage, two-strike grip, hulls never sunk by creatures | Implemented and tested |
| Regular aquatic mobs | Nibblers, puffers, lancers: 25 in six regions | Implemented and tested |
| Leviathan: bigger, chases, breaches | 2.2 times the size, hunts boats, breaches, reacts to explosions | Implemented and tested by numbers; **the breach itself was never caught in a picture** |
| Remove mandatory gear | No treasure checks for gear | Implemented and tested (all 19) |
| Fix the Tide Vault | A front door: boardwalk, ramp, open stairway | Implemented and tested on foot |
| Flatten treasure values | Near home 4 to 5, the keys 7 to 8, the rest 9 to 11 | Implemented and tested |
| No new monetization | Nothing added; the inert Robux code is untouched | Not applicable |
| Real multiplayer testing | Only one Studio client was available | **Not done** |

## 2. Verified Git branch and PR base

V7 (PR #17, branch `feature/v7-skyfall-competitive-archipelago`) was still open and unmerged when V8 started, so V8 is branch `feature/v8-chaos-and-counterplay`, cut from the V7 branch at `fcd580c`, and its pull request is opened **against the V7 branch**, not `main`. Nothing was force-pushed and nothing was merged.

The prompt asks for `docs/AI_CONTEXT.md` to be read and updated. That file no longer exists: since the October 12 consolidation the single game description is `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md`, which is what was read and updated.

## 3. Skyship aiming changes

V7 aimed a cannon at the island picked on the map and let the player nudge it 14 degrees. V8: climb in and **look**. The mouse (or `W A S D`) turns a camera above the cannon; whatever the middle of the screen is on is the aim, and the gold ring is where the flight will first touch, worked out by the same model that flies it. The client sends that point; the server works out the throw (`Dive.solve`), so a cannon cannot be asked to throw harder than it can. Past its reach (3,560 studs; the farthest island is 3,130) the ring turns red and shows the farthest it throws that way. While aiming from the ship, the ship itself is hidden so the sea below is in view, and each of the sixteen major islands wears its name and difficulty. The map still helps: `M`, click an island, and the cannon turns to it. Click or `Space` fires after a 0.5 s fuse; `X` climbs out.

Measured: aimed at open sea 1,216 studs away, first touch 42 studs short (3%). Aimed with real key presses and a real map click at Crystal Isle, the read-out named the island and the distance. Two faults found while testing are in section 19 (the hazy view, and the default aim).

## 4. Wing traversal

Each side rail has a gate amidships that opens onto a wing: a 40 by 64 stud canvas deck rising 8 degrees, a plank walkway down its middle and a diving board at the tip. Walked with the goblin's own movement from the deck through the gate to the board and back (five legs, all reached, standing on planks the whole way). Walking off the board starts a free dive: tumble, three bounces, swim.

![The ship with its wings](2026-10-13-v8-wings.jpg)

## 5. Ragdoll/floppy limb implementation

While a goblin tumbles (no keys held), its shoulders, elbows, hips and knees are switched off on the server and the limbs hang from ball sockets, so they flail as the body spins end over end. The moment the player holds glide or dive the joints come back and the goblin strikes a pose (arms out, or arms and legs in a line). Joints are disabled, never destroyed; the neck and waist are untouched, so nothing can break or kill. Landing, death, leaving and the raid's reset restore them.

Found while building it: this place's avatars use Roblox's newer `AnimationConstraint` joints, which already carry a ball socket each, and none of the older `Motor6D`. (V7's dive pose wrote to `Motor6D` only, so it never showed here.) Both kinds are handled.

Measured over a full cannon flight: 8 joints loose while tumbling, 0 while gliding or diving, all 15 joints on after landing, health 100 throughout, limbs never more than 3.6 studs from the body. On the first run limbs stretched 15.8 studs at each water bounce (the body is moved to the surface in one step); they are now hooked back on for that step.

**Not tested:** what a second player sees. The switch is made on the server so that everyone should see the same thing, but there was nobody else to look.

## 6. Water bounce and glide changes

**Bounces.** A fast goblin skips off the sea up to three times: 95, 66 and 40 studs/s upward (about 75, 36 and 13 studs high), keeping 45% of its speed across and never more than 150 studs/s, so three skips add at most about 650 studs. Half a second of grace after each bounce. The fourth touch, a gentle arrival (under 62 studs/s) or arriving in a glide is a plain landing at the surface. Measured twice from a cannon and once from a walk off the wing: bounces 1, 2, 3 in order, each lower, then "landed" at the surface with control back.

**Glide.** V7's glide held 175 studs/s for as long as there was height, so it was the way to travel. Now the throw gives the distance and the glide is a brake: the fall eases to 55 studs/s and the speed across bleeds to 50. Measured: opened at 1,066 studs out and 467 up, the goblin came down 480 studs further on, on its feet, with no ostrich landing. Hold `Shift` instead and it dives: measured 411 studs/s down, landing 210 studs short of the aim, head first.

## 7. Catapult integration

The three island catapults (Crossroads Ruins, Sun Temple, Fort Barnacle) are now launchers on the same system as the ship's cannons: `E` to climb in, look, `Space`. Each starts aimed at the place it was built to reach, so `E` then `Space` still makes the old throw. They lob at 60 degrees (at 44 they could not clear the walls). Measured, each on its own target: landed 30, 23 and 23 studs from the aim point, on top of what was there, head first, popped out, health 100. A catapult tips a goblin out after 25 s so nobody can sit in one.

## 8. Boat jump and super-jump mechanics

`Space` at any speed: a hop of about 18 studs (V7: 8.5), 0.9 s in the air. Faster than 150 studs/s (so: boosting, on a hoop chain, out of a drift) the jump grows with speed. Measured on the server's own simulation: 38.9 studs high and 201 studs flown at 187 studs/s, level the whole way. **Measured with a real driver** (I boarded with `E`, held `W`, pressed `Shift` then `Space`): top speed 188, 37.7 studs up, 1.2 s in the air, never tilted past 0.99 upright, hull untouched, no anti-cheat strike, still at the wheel.

Not separately tested in V8: a jump straight after a drift, landing a super jump on land, and re-entering water from land. The boat's land handling is V7's and was not changed.

## 9. Guardian pursuit architecture

`server/Pursuit.lua`. When a goblin carrying an island's treasure is on the water more than 70 studs off that island's shore, the island sends its sea form. Rules every form shares: one per island and five at once in the whole sea; a tell before every strike and a rest after; a leash measured from the shore; a 50 s limit; it goes home when the treasure is banked, dropped or taken, or the thief has been ashore 5 s; any explosion near it makes it reel for 4 s and the second sends it home; a strike that misses earns only 1.6 s of rest so one dodge is not the end; the raid's reset removes it. Two kinds of body: **swimmers and riders** (a small model moved over or under the waves, steering round land) and **lobbers** (creatures that cannot leave their island throw things, each shot marked on the water first). The sea mobs and the Leviathan use the same tools (`Pursuit.hit`, `batter`, `swim`, `lead`).

## 10. Island-by-island guardian pursuit roster

Each row was run once: the goblin was given that island's treasure in a skiff just off its shore and sailed straight for home at cruising speed for 15 s, doing nothing clever. "Set out" is how long the island took to respond.

| Island | Creature on land | Sea form | Set out | What happened in the run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windmill Hills | Bramble the ram | Bramble in a washtub | 0.2 s | Bleated, charged, rammed the boat (10 hull), grip slipped once, treasure kept |
| Tangle Isle | The imps | The imps' raft | 0.0 s | Drew alongside, leap called off as the boat pulled away; no hit |
| Shipwreck Shoals | Old Clacker | Clacker under the water | 0.1 s | Ring, came up through it; the boat had already left the ring |
| Tide Vault | The Warden eel | The Warden at sea | 0.0 s | Closed to 34 studs, lashed, just missed |
| Coral Atoll | The clam | The clam, jetting | 0.0 s | Reached the hull in 1.6 s and clamped for 4 s; no hull damage |
| Maelstrom Rock | The Maw | The wandering whirlpool | 0.1 s | Followed slowly; the boat outran it (closest 95 studs) |
| Crystal Isle | The Echo | The Echo on your wake | 0.0 s | Struck at once from a standing start (fixed: it now waits before following) |
| Fort Barnacle | The garrison | The garrison's launch | 0.0 s | Hung back 84 studs, two near misses (1 and 3 hull) |
| Sun Temple | The Guardian | Boulders from the temple | 0.0 s | One near miss (2 hull), grip slipped once, treasure kept |
| Crossroads Ruins | The Watchers | The walking beam | 0.0 s | Marks walked across the water; no hull damage by design |
| Ember Isle | The Cinderlings | Fire on the water | 0.2 s | Two fire patches crossed (2 hull each), grip slipped once |
| Frost Spire | The Chill | Ice on the water | 0.1 s | Ice set ahead; the boat was not caught |
| Leviathan's Rest | The Sleeper | The Leviathan | section 13 | section 13 |
| Skull Rock | The Captain's Shade | The Ghost Fleet (V4) | not re-run | Unchanged from V7 |

In no run did a pursuer strip the treasure by itself, sink the boat or kill the goblin. In the first version of the Fort run the launch's second shot dropped the treasure; its shots (and the Watchers') no longer touch the grip. Counterplay tested: an explosion on Bramble made him reel, and the framework's limit of two was confirmed in the Leviathan's version of the same rule (three). **Not tested:** each creature's original island behaviour after these changes (their island code was not edited, apart from the Sleeper), a pursuer with two carriers to choose from, and any of this with a human at the wheel.

## 11. Guardian attack and protection rebalancing

`server/Impact.lua` and `Loot.knockLoose`: after a world hit lands, nothing else from the world lands on that goblin for 1.2 s; world damage is 55% of what each source asks for; one hit cannot kill a goblin above 30 health; a hit on a carrier loosens the grip for 6 s and only a second hit in that time drops the treasure, after which it cannot be stripped again for 10 s. The Guardian's leap is the one hit that still drops at once. World blasts bite hulls at 60% and cannot take one below 12%; the Navy is exempt. PvP is unchanged. Measured on a carrying goblin: hit one landed (health 100 to 89, grip slipping, still carrying), a second hit inside the grace did nothing, a third after the grace dropped it, two more inside the recovery did not strip it again, the Guardian's leap dropped at once, and 500 damage on 60 health left 1.

## 12. Aquatic mob types and placement

Nibblers (latch and gnaw; a jump shakes them off), puffers (bounce your boat into the air, harmlessly), lancers (mark a line, then spear down it). Twenty-five, placed once by a fixed seed: The Crossing 3 puffers and 1 nibbler; Western Shallows 3 nibblers and 1 puffer; Eastern Reach 2 lancers and 2 puffers; The Open Sea 3 puffers and 2 lancers; The Far North 2 nibblers and 2 lancers; The Cinders 2 puffers, 1 lancer, 1 nibbler. None in Home Bay or Navy Waters; the nearest to the Hoard is 1,086 studs away; none within 150 studs of a shore. Measured: a puffer threw the boat up with no damage; nibblers chased, latched after 1.4 s, took 15 hull over 5 s and let go; with a jump they were off in 0.6 s for 2 hull; a lancer aimed for 1.1 s, charged, and in one run hit (6 hull, grip slipped) and in another missed. A raid's end sends them all home. The puffer's lift was raised from 86 to 140 after the first run (it was only a hop's worth); the new height was not re-measured.

## 13. Leviathan scale, attacks, movement, and activation instructions

![The Leviathan beside a skiff](2026-10-13-v8-leviathan.jpg)

**Scale:** 2.2 times V7: the head is 48 by 31 by 57 studs, with nine humps behind it.

**How to trigger it (either works):**
1. Sail to Leviathan's Rest (far north-west). Off its east dock is the Sleeper's eye. Drive a boat faster than 45 studs/s within 240 studs of it for about two seconds. The banner reads "THE LEVIATHAN IS AWAKE. IT IS COMING."
2. Steal the Leviathan Tooth and put to sea within 90 s.

**Movement:** 165 studs/s (a cruising skiff does 135, a boost 215), in wide turns; it surges to 260 when the boat is more than 260 studs ahead. **The wake:** boats within 62 studs of its head are thrown aside, no damage. **The breach:** within 220 studs it sinks, a 30-stud ring opens where the boat is going to be, and 1.6 s later the head comes up through it; a boat on the ring is thrown into the air and battered, never sunk. It picks the nearest crewed boat again after each breach. **It gives up** after 55 s, 2,400 studs from home, in water under 9 studs deep, or after three explosions on its head.

Measured, one skiff: sailing straight and doing nothing, breached twice (7 and 15 hull) and left behind at the leash after 16 s. Boosting and super-jumping when the ring opened: 35 studs up, hull untouched. Three blasts on its head: it reeled three times and went home. A raid ending mid-hunt: gone.

Found while testing: it was being stepped twice a frame whenever the Sleeper was awake, so it moved at double speed; fixed. **Not verified:** the breach as a picture (I never caught the 2 seconds on a screenshot, so I cannot say it looks right, only that it hits and can be dodged); the shallow-water escape (the test boat never reached shallow water); more than one boat.

## 14. Removed equipment requirements

The Rebreather, Cinder Boots and Frost Claws still exist and still help (breath, fire, grip). The server no longer checks for them, the map no longer says "+ GEAR", and the refusal message is gone. Measured: with no gear, all 19 treasures were taken on their spots, including the Pearl of the Deep, the Ember Crown and the Aurora Gem. **Not re-walked in V8:** the paths to the Ember Crown and the Aurora Gem (V7's route tests stand; the paths were not changed).

## 15. Tide Vault access fix

Three playtests could not find the way in: it was a tunnel on the far side from the dock, behind a gate whose lever stood 100 studs away. Now a boardwalk runs from the dock to the north ramp, and at the top of the ramp an open stairway goes down to the pearl, which glows under a skylight. No gate, no lever, no gear. Taking the pearl floods the vault to just below the top of the stairs, so the way out is the way in. Measured on foot with the goblin's own movement: dock to pearl in 5.0 s; `E` stole it with the camera deliberately turned away; the vault flooded; out to the dock again carrying it in 5.4 s, health 100. Separately, the same pearl banked at the Hoard for 10 gold. **Not done as one unbroken run:** sailing it home from the Tide Vault dock (boats and banking are V7's code).

## 16. New treasure reward table

| Treasure | Island | V7 value | V8 value | V7 respawn (s) | V8 respawn (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lost Compass | Pebble Isle | 1 | 4 | 20 | 150 |
| Giant Pearl | Coral Atoll | 2 | 5 | 25 | 160 |
| Smuggler's Stash | Smuggler's Cove | 2 | 5 | 25 | 160 |
| Sunken Sextant | Kelp Cay | 4 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Storm Lantern | Lantern Key | 9 | 8 | 45 | 60 |
| Castaway's Hoard | Driftwood Key | 9 | 8 | 45 | 60 |
| Golden Gear | Windmill Hills | 4 | 9 | 30 | 60 |
| Lighthouse Lens | Crossroads Ruins | 4 | 9 | 25 | 60 |
| Captain's Chest | Shipwreck Shoals | 5 | 9 | 35 | 60 |
| Crystal Heart | Crystal Isle | 7 | 10 | 40 | 60 |
| Jade Frog | Tangle Isle | 9 | 10 | 40 | 60 |
| Pearl of the Deep | Tide Vault | 8 | 10 | 45 | 60 |
| Tempest Trident | Maelstrom Rock | 8 | 10 | 45 | 60 |
| Ember Crown | Ember Isle | 13 | 10 | 50 | 60 |
| Admiral's Strongbox | Fort Barnacle | 13 | 11 | 50 | 70 |

| Leviathan Tooth | Leviathan's Rest | 17 | 11 | 70 | 70 |

V7's values were read from the V7 commit (`fcd580c`); V8's were read back from the running server. V7 ran from 1 to 20 gold, so the far islands were the only sensible choice; V8 runs from 4 to 11. The three nearest home are worth about half and take two and a half minutes to come back (V7: 20 to 25 s), so they cannot win by repetition. Interest still adds up to three steps of about 12% to anything left untouched (seen in play: the Idol at 13, the Strongbox at 14), and the final rush still pays 25% more.

## 17. Multiplayer and performance considerations

**Authority.** A launcher is aimed at a point and the server works out the velocity. Hits, grip, hull damage and treasure are all decided on the server. The goblin's own client flies its own flight (as it drives its own boat); the server rules on how it ends and ends any flight after 45 s. A cheating client could fly its own character where it likes, which is true of every Roblox character and not new.

**Cost.** Server frame time with a pursuit running: 0.87 ms. Sea mobs: 25 bodies of 4 to 8 welded parts, moved only when a crewed boat is near (a sweep four times a second decides). Pursuers: at most 5, one small model each. The Leviathan: about 26 anchored parts moved each frame while it is awake. None of it grows with the number of players. The threats folder holds 326 parts in all.

**Not established:** anything about 32 players. One client cannot show replication cost, how two flights look to each other, or how five pursuits and a Leviathan hunt feel on a busy server.

## 18. Studio tests actually performed

All in Roblox Studio play mode, one client, through the built-in Studio MCP. Real key and mouse input was used where marked.

- **Skyship:** walked the wing and back (own movement); climbed into a cannon with `E` (real key); aimed with `W A S D` (real keys) and with a map click (real mouse); fired with `Space` (real key); tumble to three bounces; glide held from mid-flight (real key) to a soft landing; dive held (real key) to an ostrich landing; walked off the diving board; left aboard until the window closed and was fired off; ended a raid while seated in a boat and was put back on deck.
- **Catapults:** all three, on their own targets, traced to landing.
- **Boats:** hop and super jump on the server's simulation; a super jump with a real driver (real keys), with the anti-cheat's counters read afterwards.
- **Pursuit:** twelve forms, one 15 s run each (section 10); the reset.
- **Sea mobs:** placement listed; puffer, nibbler (with and without a jump), lancer (twice).
- **Leviathan:** five hunts (straight, boosting, jumping, with blasts, toward the island) plus two after tuning.
- **Treasure:** all 19 taken with no gear; values read back; the Tide Vault walked in and out; one bank.
- **Impact:** the grip sequence on a carrying goblin.
- **Checks:** StyLua and Selene clean; `scripts/check.ps1` result is in the pull request.

**Not performed:** anything with a second client; a human playing; a full raid from start to finish; the Ember and Frost paths on foot; each creature's island behaviour; touch or gamepad for the new aim.

## 19. Bugs found and fixed

1. `E` cast Poltergoblin instead of stealing when the camera was turned away from a treasure in reach (Roblox only shows prompts that are on screen). `E` now acts on anything in reach.
2. A storm's lightning struck goblins on the skyship 540 studs up and killed one sitting in a cannon. Weather now ignores anyone above 200 studs.
3. Loose limbs stretched 15 studs at each water bounce. Fixed (section 5).
4. The aim view was a fog: forty layers of nearly clear deck and sail, plus the ship's glow. The ship is now hidden outright while aiming.
5. Island name tags did not draw with "always on top" in the views I could capture; they are ordinary signs now.
6. Catapults fell 60 to 90 studs short at 44 degrees (walls and cliffs). Now 60 degrees.
7. A launcher's starting aim was replaced within a tenth of a second by whatever slope was in the middle of the screen, so `E` then `Space` on a catapult landed on the hillside below its target. It now stays exactly on its starting aim until turned.
8. The Leviathan moved at double speed whenever the Sleeper was awake (stepped twice a frame).
9. A goblin at a boat's wheel when the raid ended was not put back on the skyship: their own client still held them in the seat, the move was undone, and the ship "dived" them into the seabed. It now retries until it takes.
10. Pursuits never started off the bigger islands because the leash was measured from the island's middle. Now from its shore.
11. The Echo struck a boat at once from a standing start. It now waits its delay before following.
12. Mine, in testing only: my chase test left the last treasure in the goblin's hands, so every run after the first tested nothing. The first full set of pursuit results was thrown away and re-run.

## 20. Known issues and limitations

- No human has played this and it has never had two players. That is the largest limitation and it applies to everything above.
- The sea forms and mobs are a handful of blocks and balls each. They read as what they are from a boat; they are not art.
- The Leviathan's breach was not seen in a still image.
- Pursuers steer round land with a look-ahead, not along routes; among tight rocks one can stall until its time runs out.
- Lobbers (boulders, beam, fire, ice) cannot be driven off with explosions; the answer is to get out of range.
- A first strike often misses a boat that is still accelerating from rest, because the tell is aimed at where the boat was heading. That is intended as dodge room; it may prove too forgiving.
- My test boat, driven blind in a straight line, crashed into islands near the end of several runs (about 70 hull each time). That is my test, not the game, but it means the hull numbers at the very end of those runs are not the creatures' doing.
- The old client code for catapult pads is unreachable and still present.
- The new aim has no gamepad stick or touch control. Keyboard and mouse only.
- `AGENTS.md` still lists progression and pets as excluded before prototype approval (raised in V7's pull request; a human decision). V8 added none.

## 21. Incomplete or deferred features

- **Multiplayer testing of any kind.** Not possible here.
- **Other players seeing the loose limbs.** Built to replicate, never observed.
- **The Leviathan with two boats, and its shallow-water escape.** Built, not observed.
- **A boat-form Guardian.** The Guardian throws boulders from its temple instead; it does not swim or sail.
- **A new sea form for the Captain's Shade.** The Ghost Fleet already hunts the thief and was left as it is.
- **Creatures reacting to each other, or to the Navy.** Not attempted.
- **Sound by ear.** The new effects reuse existing sounds; I cannot hear them.

## 22. Human playtest instructions

Double-click **Play Loot Goblins**, wait for Studio, press the blue Play button, press `H` for the help panel. Then try these and say what felt bad:

1. **The cannon.** Climb in (`E`), move the mouse, watch the gold ring. Fire at an island on purpose. Did you land where the ring was?
2. **The air.** Fire again and touch nothing. Then hold `Space` near the ground. Then hold `Shift`. Aim one at open water on purpose.
3. **The wings.** Walk out of the gate in the rail, to the end of the diving board, and off.
4. **A catapult** (Crossroads Ruins, on the crag): `E`, look somewhere else, `Space`.
5. **The boat.** `Space` at cruising speed, then `Shift` and `Space` together.
6. **Steal the Golden Gear** (Windmill Hills) and sail away. Something follows. Try a jump when it bleats.
7. **Steal anything from Coral Atoll** and sail away. When something grabs the hull, jump.
8. **The Tide Vault**: land at its dock and follow the boardwalk. No gear.
9. **The Leviathan**: sail fast past the east dock of Leviathan's Rest. Then run.
10. **Run into a puffer fish** (yellow, spiky, floating) on purpose.

The fourteen questions the team asked, to answer after playing:

1. Is skydiving substantially funnier and more intuitive?
2. Can you aim the skyship cannons at the island you actually want?
3. Are the three water bounces enjoyable?
4. Is gliding better balanced?
5. Are the improved boat jumps fun?
6. Do creatures following you into the water make memorable situations?
7. Do the creatures in boats feel hilarious or annoying?
8. Is the Leviathan intimidating and enjoyable to escape?
9. Do you keep control during chaotic encounters?
10. Are treasure drops and deaths less frustrating?
11. Is the Tide Vault now straightforward?
12. Does removing the gear requirement improve the loop?
13. Do similar treasure values make island choice more natural?
14. Are the sea mobs entertaining without making the ocean exhausting?

Send a screenshot of any red error. None of the checks in this report can answer these questions.

## 23. Recommended next priorities

1. **Play it, with three people.** Every number here is a guess at fun until then.
2. Watch the loose limbs and two simultaneous flights from a second client; that is the most likely place for a surprise.
3. Tune pursuit pressure from play: whether first strikes miss too easily, and whether five at once is too many or too few.
4. Look at the Leviathan's breach with human eyes and give it a proper body if the hunt earns its place.
5. Decide whether the lobbers need a counter other than distance.
6. Remove the unreachable catapult-pad code once the launchers are accepted.

## Report: 2026-10-13-v7-skyfall-competitive-archipelago.md

# V7: Skyfall and the competitive archipelago (October 13, 2026)

Branch `feature/v7-skyfall-competitive-archipelago`, cut from `origin/main` at `92c5e7d` (V6 had already been merged: PR #14 at `ef315ff`, with the Skull Chalice repair). PR against `main`; **not merged**. Built by Claude (Sonnet 5.5) in one autonomous session from the V7 one-shot prompt after the first multiplayer playtest of V6.

**Everything below was tested by one AI on one Studio client.** That includes everything about "multiplayer": see section 22. Nothing here has been played by a person. Where a thing is only code, it says so.

## 0. Plan and what was decided

Order of work: foundation (round length, map, routes), boats, fighting, skyship, world systems (alerts, gear, Leviathan), progression, interface, then tests and this report. The prompt asks for progression, pets and monetization, which `AGENTS.md` still lists as excluded "before prototype approval". The prompt is an explicit instruction from the team, so they were built, but **`AGENTS.md` was not edited** (rules need human review): Enrik should decide whether that line is now out of date.

## 1. Summary

| Grapple catches, E steals | Implemented; tested with a stand-in thief (no second player) |

| White Navy | Implemented; not looked at |

| Final rush, route fixes | Implemented and tested |

## 2. Git

Fetched `origin`: V5 and V6 branches were gone and `main` held V6. `main` was fast-forwarded (local copy was clean), `feature/v7-skyfall-competitive-archipelago` created from it. Commits `2e05aa9` (part 1: sea, boats, grapple, skyship), `466dc4c` (part 2: alerts, gear, progression, Leviathan, route fixes), `099ab1b` (part 3: final rush, interface, laps) and this documentation commit, all pushed normally. No force-push, nothing merged, `main` untouched. The gameplay revision this report describes is `099ab1b`.

## 3. Map

Every island beyond the home ring moved 20% farther from Goblin Cove along the same line (`Archipelago.lua`), keeping its size and Twin Stacks' offset from Crystal Isle. Sea 5,880 by 5,010 studs (V6: 5,080 by 4,390). Farthest island, Skull Rock: 4,544 studs from home (V6: 3,724). A skiff now does 135, so the crossing is 33.6 s (V6: 34.5 s at 108). Region labels moved with it; "THE LONG REACH" became "THE OPEN SEA". After the move the build was clean (`verify`: nothing stranded, all 43 boats afloat, 11 ziplines clear, no coin on land, no warnings), and every sea feature followed because all of them are placed from island positions.

## 4. The sixteen major islands

A major island has a treasure, something living or moving on it, and a tier computed from five 0 to 3 factors (guardian, traversal, hazard, extraction, gear). The tier is the sum: 0 to 3 EASY, 4 to 6 RISKY, 7 to 9 DANGEROUS, 10 up DEADLY. It is shown on the map under each name.

| Island | Tier | Challenge | Needs gear |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pebble Isle | EASY | Navigation | |
| Coral Atoll | EASY | Timing (the clam) | |
| Smuggler's Cove | EASY | Stealth (the bell) | |
| Windmill Hills | RISKY | Timing (blades, the ram) | |
| Crossroads Ruins | RISKY | Stealth (the Watchers) | |
| Shipwreck Shoals | RISKY | Environment (crab, wreck guns) | |
| Crystal Isle | RISKY | Terrain (cave-in, the Echo) | |
| Tangle Isle | DANGEROUS | Speed (bridges, imps) | |
| Tide Vault | DANGEROUS | Equipment (the flood) | Diver's Rebreather |
| Maelstrom Rock | DANGEROUS | Boat skill | |
| Fort Barnacle | DEADLY | Combat (marines, chain) | |
| Ember Isle | DEADLY | Equipment (lava) | Cinder Boots |
| Sun Temple | DEADLY | Combat (the Guardian) | |
| Frost Spire | DEADLY | Equipment (the Chill) | Frost Claws |
| Leviathan's Rest | DEADLY | Boss | |
| Skull Rock | DEADLY | Stealth (the ghost fleet) | |

This is 3 easy, 4 risky, 3 dangerous and 6 deadly: heavy at the top, on purpose, because that is where the gold is. Nothing was deleted. **Supporting geography kept:** Gull Rock, Twin Stacks, Pilgrim's Rock (nothing to take); Kelp Cay, Lantern Key, Driftwood Key keep their small treasure (Sextant 4, Lantern 9, Castaway's Hoard 9) and the first two hold the gear caches. The three keys were the consolidated "treasure islands": their loot is unchanged and they are no longer counted among the majors.

## 5. Skyship deployment

`server/Skyship.lua`, `client/Skyship.lua`, `shared/Dive.lua`. A ship (about 290 parts: deck, masts, sails, wings, a glowing belly, twelve cannons) hangs at (0, 540, -80), centre of the sea. It is in the persistent `Landmarks` folder. At raid end everyone is put on the deck for the intermission; the raid clock starts at the same moment the cannons unlock (3 s later). A 28 s window follows; anyone still aboard is fired at their chosen island (or a near one) when it ends. A goblin who jumps off the side is a free dive. Respawns and late arrivals during the window start aboard; after it, at the cove.

How a goblin plays it: the map opens by itself (click an island: shown with its tier, a coloured beam stands over it), walk to a cannon and press E, A/D turn and W/S tilt (within 14 and 10 degrees), a ring and two arcs show where a glide (green) and a pencil dive (orange) end, Space fires after a 0.9 s fuse, X climbs out.

Tested: boarding, the map opening, clicking an island (server saw `Cross`), E at a cannon (`loaded`), Space (fuse, launch 210 studs/s at +94), the aim camera, free dive off the side, and the whole fall.

## 6. Dive and landing

One small model in `shared/Dive.lua` (a velocity relaxing toward a target), used by the flying client and by the landing preview. Pencil: 55 along, 150 down. Glide (Space held): 175 along, 30 down, 5.7 studs of reach per stud of height. The cannon throws at 230 and the velocity settles within about two seconds.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Pencil dive from the cannon at the Crossroads | Launch 0.8 s after Space, down at 152 studs/s, ground at 5.5 s |
| Ground at pencil speed (impact 95 or more) | Head first, anchored upside down 1.1 s with a wiggle, popped out at 62 up, control back (`landed`) |
| Glide, Space held, aimed at Maelstrom Rock (2,500 studs) | Over it in 17 s at a steady 175 and 33 down; soft landing at y 28 |
| Free dive over open sea | Water at 4.2 s: bounce up at 135; first version bounced only 10 studs and re-detected the water as a second landing |

Fixed during testing: the diver collided with its own cannon and rail (two collision groups: divers pass through the ship only); the bounce got its own ballistic arc (about 100 studs) and a 0.8 s grace; the aim camera sat inside the barrel.

One screenshot of a real pencil dive from the player's own view is `2026-10-13-v7-pencil-dive.jpg` next to this report (head first over the sea, island names and hoops below, the banner reading "PENCIL DIVE (hold SPACE to glide)", the distance to the chosen island and the height). **Not verified:** the glide pose, the arms (the screenshot shows them at the sides, not overhead), other players diving.

![A pencil dive](2026-10-13-v7-pencil-dive.jpg)

The map as a goblin sees it aboard the ship (islands with their difficulty word and gear, a storm over Ember Isle): `2026-10-13-v7-map.jpg`.

## 7. Boats

Skiff 108 to 135, cutter 86 to 104, patrol ship 88 to 106. Turn rate and its fade with speed were changed so a skiff at chain speed turns about as tightly as V6's did. Boost: 1.5 times (202), a 14 studs/s kick at the start, 5 s cooldown. Chains: up to five links, ceiling 242. Drift bursts and clean landings kick harder.

| Measure (skiff, server sim) | V6 | V7 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top speed | 108 | 135 (121 at 3 s) |
| Boosted peak | 151 | 194 in the test (202 limit) |
| Turn radius at cruise | | 84 studs at 118 studs/s |
| Turn radius boosted | about 180 at 165 | 146 at 173 |

With the player's own client driving (keys W, Space, Shift, X on a skiff from the cove): cruise to about 124, a Space hop to 8.7 studs up and back down in 0.6 s (the seat did not eject), Shift to 191, X leaves the seat.

## 8. Jump and land driving

`Space` at the wheel hops the boat (58 studs/s up, 1.3 s cooldown, needs water or ground under it). A second press inside the cooldown was refused. A jump from a charged drift releases the burst. A plain hop never gives the landing kick (that needs 0.7 s in the air: a ramp or a boosted jump). Landing on land is a thump, never a burst.

On land a boat drives at 30% of its top speed (about 22 studs/s measured on the flat by the Hoard, a skiff's cap is 40), steers and reverses. A boost does not raise it. On a steep (32 degree) beach it climbs the gentle part and stops at the step, and reversing takes it back to sea: it did not wedge. A boat hitting a beach at speed still takes hull damage.

## 9. Recall (B)

The nearest free boat sails in; with none free a skiff is built (at most six extra, oldest retired). The boat is placed 520 studs out in open water and drives itself in under the same physics, with a green beam on it. Cooldown 45 s, not while seated, not with a boat within 70 studs, a Tug Crab shortens it. Tested: from Kelp Cay a dock boat 480 studs away arrived in 6 s (server call), and with the real B key a boat 390 studs away arrived in 5. Not tested: simultaneous calls, a sunk boat on the way, two goblins on one boat.

## 10. Grapple and theft

F within 40 studs of a carrier (V6: 70, and it stole at once) **catches** them: yanked toward the thrower, knocked down 2 s, nothing stolen. The thrower runs up and presses E within 8 studs: the server checks the thief, the distance, the wall, the hold and the throw cooldown, and takes the treasure only then. Space after 0.9 s gets the victim up; after getting up nobody can be caught for 6 s. The pull to walls, ground and boats keeps its 170 stud range. Loose treasure is still grabbed at 70.

Tested on the server with a stand-in thief (a rig that behaves like a player) and the real goblin as the victim, carrying: a steal while standing refused; catch from 30 studs landed (down 1.9 s, cooldown 4.5); a second catch while down changed nothing; a steal from 30 studs refused; **a steal from 4 studs with 0.68 s of down time left took the treasure** (the victim stood up, immune); a catch while immune refused; full recovery; Space too early ignored, after 0.9 s it worked; a catch inside the Hoard's ring refused. **Not tested:** two real players, latency, the prompt appearing on a real body, a wall in the way.

## 11. Controls and cannons

Final scheme: on foot unchanged (Shift sprint, C dash, Space air jump, E steal or interact, F hook, Q throw, G keg, E with no prompt Poltergoblin); at the wheel W/S/A/D, Shift boost, C drift, **Space hop, X leave, B call a boat**; M map, H help, **T all treasure, P locker**. Gamepad: A, Y, X, B and D-pad down are bound for the new actions. Touch: no new buttons (as before). Every cannon prompt now shows a ring where the shot goes (green ready, red reloading) and READY or the seconds left. **Not done:** a trajectory arc for the island and boat cannons (only the skyship's cannons have one).

## 12. Navigation and interface

Carrying: an arrow on a ring round the middle of the screen points at the Hoard with the distance (hidden within 90 studs). The compass strip lists only treasure within 1,300 studs and none while carrying. The treasure board shows only what is loose or carried, `T` shows all. The map shows tier and gear, who is on guard (red ring) and the chosen landing. The help panel (H) was rewritten. Not seen on screen: the arrow, the compact board.

## 13. Competition

Alerts (section 14), the final rush (last 90 s, banking pays 25% more: tested, an Idol banked for 18), the gear choice, and Shinies that reward trying (section 18). **Not done:** a live standings panel beyond Roblox's own player list; a comeback mechanic inside the raid beyond the rush.

## 14. Regional alerts

`server/Alerts.lua`. A theft puts its island on guard (level 0 to 3, falling 1 per 40 s) and linked islands (`Config.ALERT.LINKS`) by a weight. At level 1 or more creatures wake from 30% farther per level. At level 2 every patrol ship within 1,800 studs turns toward the island for 35 s, so the rest of the sea is quieter. Heat is untouched. Tested: a theft at the Fort gave Fort 1, a second gave Fort 2 and Tangle 1, the attribute `Alert_Fort` was published, the wake factor read 1.6, and everything fell to 0 in 60 s. **Not tested:** a patrol ship actually turning, and the map ring on screen.

## 15. Leviathan

`server/Leviathan.lua`, driven by the Sleeper's own tick. Seven humps swim a circle off the east dock and rise as awareness grows; when the Sleeper strikes, a head and a twelve-segment neck arc 74 studs up and come down on the marked circle exactly as the marker closes (6 studs off in the test). A blast on the head (a keg, a cannonball) makes it recoil and sink: the head fell 24 studs in 0.45 s. The damage, markers and telegraphs are the old strike's. No health bar. **Not looked at.**

## 16. Equipment

Rebreather (Kelp Cay, swim 1.4 times: 24 to 33.5 measured), Cinder Boots (Lantern Key, fire, lava and lava bombs do nothing), Frost Claws (Lantern Key, the Chill drains a quarter as much); Lantern Key offers boots or claws. Without the piece the treasure on Tide Vault, Ember Isle and Frost Spire is refused (checked: the message names the piece and where to find it); no gear for Cross was allowed. Free in the world; Shinies can buy "start with it". **Not tested by hand:** picking up from a cache, boots against real lava, claws against the Chill.

## 17. Shinies, pets and Robux

`Progress.lua`, `Shop.lua`, `Monetization.lua`. Raid Gold wins the raid; **Shinies** are kept. A raid pays 10 for being there 90 s, 1 per gold banked (to 30), 25 for winning, 5 to a goblin who banked something and sits at or below the middle, at most 70.

Tested against a stand-in store: one payout per raid (47 for 12 gold and a win), none a second time, buying (refused when too poor, refused twice, refused for an invented id), equip, a save, a failing store (kept dirty, `SaveState = unsaved`, saved when it came back), a receipt granted once and answered twice, an unknown product refused, **a receipt answered "not yet" when the save failed**. In Studio the real DataStore is unavailable, so `SaveState` read `unavailable` and nothing was saved: **real saving has not been run.**

Pets (one out at a time, different verbs): Tug Crab (boat calls 40% faster), Scout Gull (nearest waiting treasure and its distance), Spring Frog (dash recharges 35% faster), Shell Tortoise (the first catch every 30 s bounces off), Pocket Ghost (Poltergoblin recharges 25% faster). Tested: the attribute path; a pet is drawn on every client from the attribute (not looked at). **Monetization is inert:** `Config.MONETIZATION.PRODUCTS` is empty on purpose. To turn it on: create a Developer Product per pet in the Creator Dashboard, paste `[productId] = { pet = "Gull" }`, publish, test with a second account in a published test place. No id was invented.

**Roblox settings needed (outside the repository):** Max Players 32 in the experience settings; Studio's "Enable Studio Access to API Services" on to test saving; Developer Products for sales.

## 18. Accessibility fixes

| Report | Cause | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windmill ladder | stood 9.4 studs from the tower, under the gallery (radius 12) | 13.6 out, tops above the rim | Walked up, on the gallery in 1.5 s |
| Fort cannon stand | ladder ran into the stand's edge, then (after a first fix) topped out at floor height | beside the stand, 20 high | On the stand in 1.5 s |
| Ember crater | the funnel was cut with air slabs 2.2 studs thick; **the engine ignores an air fill thinner than a 4-stud cell**, so the volcano was solid on top since V4 | slabs 6 thick | crater centre 129.8 to 113.1; a path from the beach reaches the crown |
| Tide Vault | gate started closed, its only lever 100 studs away; drain 5 studs wide | gate starts open (the pearl still slams it), drain 8 wide | gate at 15 (open) once the raid runs; a path reaches the altar |
| Skull Rock | (V6 repair) | unchanged | Walked up the ladder in 1.2 s after the merge and the move |

## 19. Sea layout, lanes and courses

All 13 lanes driven by the autopilot at full chain speed with the new boats on the new sea: every hoop taken, speeds 218 to 243. Times: Gate Run 1.8 s, West 4.5, Mill 3.6, Chimney 5.4, Temple 3.8, Ember Road 7.6 (chain 8), Frost 4.5, Lantern 3.6, Tangle 4.9, Leviathan 4.1, Northern Drift 4.8, Tide Run 4.2. Courses: Teeth 2.8, Cinder Slalom 2.7, Serpent Run 2.2 and 2.4 reversed, both directions. The two laps were too tight for the new speed (hoops missed by 20 to 50 studs) so the radii went from 330 and 290 to 400 and 350: Lookout Loop 11.9 s clean forwards and 12.0 reversed with one hoop 3 studs outside the gate, Maelstrom Ring 10.7 and 11.0 with a hoop or two 4 to 7 studs outside. **Pars** (new, measured plus 17%): Teeth 3.3, Cinder 3.2, Serpent 2.8, Lookout 14, Maelstrom 12.8. The first Chimney Run missed a hoop by 49 studs (a short run-up); with a longer one it was clean.

## 20. Performance

World build 3.3 to 3.9 s, sea grid 3.1 to 3.4 s. Server parts 5,689 (V6: 5,382; the ship is about 290), instances 52,498, heartbeat 0.06 ms in the sample. Client 59.8 fps over 4 s at Skull Rock with 7,122 instances streamed, worst frame 18 ms, Studio's window in front. **Not measured:** a busy scene, 32 players, the dive's client cost, the new pets and rings.

## 21. Bugs found by testing

The diver stuck inside its cannon (collision groups); the water bounce too small and re-detected (own arc and grace); the aim camera inside the barrel (scripted camera); the skyship banner not started and overlapping the map; a land test that stopped because a test boat flagged as AI is removed by the raid's reset (test artifact); the stand-in thief's own body blocking the line of sight (test artifact); the home spawn pad widened from 12 to 28 studs for 32 respawns.

## 22. Multiplayer: what was and was not done

**No second player was ever in the game.** Studio's multi-client launcher could not be driven from here. So: PvP was tested with a stand-in thief; the skyship with one goblin; nothing was tested with 32 or even 2. A code audit found nothing that assumes one player: loops are over `Players:GetPlayers()`, boats are 43 plus up to 6 extras, the ship has 36 deck spots and 12 cannons (32 goblins launch in about three rounds of 0.9 s fuses: not measured), home respawn is one wide pad, Navy and creatures target carriers. **Treasure supply is the real risk:** 19 treasures for 32 players means contention and empty islands; whether that is fun is a playtest question.

## 23. Known limitations

The ship and dive have never been seen by a person; the dive pose is untested visually; no touch buttons for the new actions; the Leviathan and white Navy are unseen; the island and boat cannons have no arc; saving has only run against a stand-in; the alert's Navy effect has run without ships; Space on touch for the hop; spawning at a remote island's far side of the sea if the aim is bad costs a long swim (B helps); the skyship does not move; gear can be swapped for another only at Lantern Key.

## 24. Deferred

A live standings panel; an in-raid comeback beyond the rush; a trajectory arc for every cannon; routes that need gear (only treasure rooms do); a real stress test; pose polish; the sound of the ship (built-in sounds only).

## 25. Human playtest plan

Use **Test > Server & Clients** with several players. (1) From the first second: does the ship read, can everyone pick an island and launch without queueing, is falling funny? (2) Land on water, ground and an island in a glide. (3) Two goblins: catch, run up, E: fair? loops? (4) Boats: hop, land driving, B when stranded. (5) Rob an island: does the map ring and the Navy turn make sense? (6) Gear: Tide, Ember, Frost with and without. (7) The Leviathan: dodge it, blast its head. (8) Final rush. (9) P: buy a pet. Report what felt bad; send a screenshot of any red error.

## 26. Next priorities

A real multiplayer session with eight or more; look at the ship, the dive and the Leviathan; real DataStore save in a published test place; treasure supply for 32; touch controls; a cannon arc everywhere.
