## Report: 2026-10-12-v6-ocean-flow-audio.md

# Report: V6, ocean flow and sensory polish

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-10-12 |
| Request | Ninety's "V6 One-Shot: Ocean Flow & Sensory Polish" prompt |
| Agent | Claude Code (Opus 5.5), local session on Ninety's machine with Roblox Studio MCP |
| Branch | `feature/v6-ocean-flow-audio`, **stacked on** PR #13's branch `feature/v5-living-threats-playful-seas` (then #12, #11, #10, #9) |
| Pull request | [#14](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/14), base branch is `feature/v5-living-threats-playful-seas` |
| Merge status | **Not merged.** Nothing was merged, including PRs #9 to #13. Needs a human playtest and explicit approval. |

## 1. Summary

The V5 playtest said the map, the boats and the creatures are right, the things to do at sea are fun but badly placed, and there have been explosions in the distance since V2. V6 adds no system. It lays the sea out again and fixes the sound.

- **The sea was laid out again by a few rules** (section 3). 95 hoops (V5: 110), 132 coins (V5: 326), 6 ramps (7), 5 timed courses (6).
- **Home Bay is calm.** Within 300 studs of the harbor mouth there were 12 hoops and 34 coins. There are 3 and 3. One line of hoops runs from the harbor through the Gate to the Crossroads.
- **Lanes are straight and point at docks.** Thirteen of them. The ones that hooked round islands are gone. The western sea, which had 5 hoops, has 14.
- **Every lane and course was driven** by an autopilot using the game's own boat physics, at full hoop-chain speed, and changed until it could be followed. That found real faults: V5's two slaloms could not be threaded at speed, and a lap has to be much wider than V5's.
- **Par times are measured**, not guessed.
- **The distant explosions were thunder.** Every lightning bolt of every storm played a boom to every player, in their ears, never quieter than 15% volume. Standing at home with three storms 1,600 to 2,900 studs away: **31 booms in 38 seconds**. In V6, same place, storms that far away: **none**. A storm that actually comes near is still heard, and loudly at the strike.
- **Signs only show when they are really in range**, which takes about ten far-off island names off the horizon at home.

Tested in Studio by one AI on one client. **Nobody has played V6**, and I cannot hear: the sound was checked from logs of what was played, where, and how loud by the falloff formula. Section 12 says exactly what was and was not verified.

![The view from the harbor ramp in V5](2026-10-12-v6-harbor-before.jpg)

![The same view in V6](2026-10-12-v6-harbor-after.jpg)

## 2. What was wrong with V5's arrangement

Looked at in Studio and on an overhead map drawn from the running game (every hoop, coin and boat, over a 10-stud survey of the coastline).

![V5's sea](2026-10-12-v6-sea-before.png)

1. **A quarter of everything was in Home Bay.** 27 of 110 hoops and 80 of 326 coins, in the smallest region. The Bay Circuit's ten orange hoops sat across the harbor mouth, the Gate Run ran through the middle of them, four big coins glowed on the reef, and the signs for all of it overlapped. From the harbor ramp it was a wall.
2. **Lanes hooked round islands.** The Back Door Arc looped round the south of home. The Mill Run went north round Smuggler's Cove and then S-bent down a strait. The Ember Reach curled right round Crystal Isle. The Lantern Line and Tangle Lane had doglegs. A hoop every 120 studs made each bend a string of small course corrections.
3. **The western sea had almost nothing:** 5 hoops and 9 coins.
4. **The slaloms had never been driven, and could not be.** Driven at speed in V6's first test, a boat on the Teeth (seven gates 80 to 120 studs apart, sidestepping 25 to 55 studs between them) missed the third and fourth gates by 49 and 32 studs and hit a stack. The Cinder Slalom had a sea stack on the straight line between its second and third hoops, and ended at an empty shore.
5. **Nothing told one thing from another.** Lane hoops, course hoops and coins were everywhere at the same density.
6. **Salvage crates were dropped on top of random coins**, which put them inside slaloms, in the fort's harbor and in the bay.
7. **Thunder** (section 9).
8. **Signs showed from much farther than intended** (section 8).

## 3. The layout strategy

Four rules, written at the top of `src/server/Searuns.lua` so the next person keeps them.

- **A teal hoop is a lane.** It points at a dock across open water. It is straight unless there is a reason to bend. Hoops stand about 190 studs apart (V5: 120): far enough apart to see past, close enough to chain (a chain lasts 4 seconds; at 150 studs a second that is 600 studs). A small sign at each end says where it goes, readable only from close by.
- **An orange hoop is a timed course**: a run threaded through sea stacks, a sprint down a current, or a lap round a landmark. These are places to go and play, set apart from the lanes.
- **A coin marks a line worth taking**: a weave through a course, a stack to hug, the air over a ramp, the way into somewhere hidden. A few long lanes carry one coin between hoops. Coins never just fill water.
- **Some water is left alone.** Home Bay has one line out. The fort's water, the skull's, the east beyond Crystal Isle and the south of home have no lanes, so that they stay quiet.

One more rule came out of the driving tests and matters for anyone adding a hoop:

- **A hoop chain holds a skiff at 150 to 175 studs a second, and at that speed it barely steers.** It needs about 180 studs of radius to turn, and its course lags its bow by a moment. Measured: a boat stayed on a course whose line bent 8 degrees at a gate and left one that bent 24. So a line of hoops must hardly bend (10 degrees a gate at most, at 150 studs apart), a lap needs a radius of about 300, and **where the way really twists, do not use hoops at all**: use coins, which show the way and leave the speed to the pilot.

![V6's sea](2026-10-12-v6-sea-after.png)

## 5. The lanes

Each was driven both ways by the autopilot (section 12) at full chain. "Time" is from first hoop to last.

| Lane | From, to | Hoops | Studs | Coins | Time | What changed from V5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Gate Run** | The harbor, through the Gate, to the Crossroads' south dock | 4 | 368 | 0 | 2.4 s | Dead straight through the middle of the Gate. No longer runs through a circuit. No coins: the bay is calm. |
| **West Run** | Outside Gull Pass to Shipwreck Shoals' dock | 4 | 575 | 3 | 3.8 s | Straight. Starts outside the reef. The West Jump is still beside it. |
| **Mill Run** | East out of the bay, south of Smuggler's Cove, to Windmill Hills' west dock | 4 | 493 | 0 | 3.2 s | V5 went north round Smuggler's Cove and S-bent down the strait. Now a straight line. The Mill Race current, just south, is the way back. |
| **Chimney Run** | Smuggler's Gap, past the Chimney, to Crystal Isle's west dock | 5 | 771 | 4 | 5.2 s | New. |
| **Temple Run** | The Crossroads' north dock, past Pilgrim's Rock, to the temple's dock | 4 | 475 | 0 | 3.2 s | Was the timed "Pilgrim's Run". It is the main way north, so it is a lane now. |
| **Ember Road** | North of the Crossroads across the open reach to Ember Isle's west beach | 7 | 1215 | 6 | 7.8 s | New. The long one: nothing in the way, a chain of 6, top speed 175. Replaces the Reach Run and the Ember Reach. |
| **Frost Road** | The temple's east coast, past the Two Sisters, to Frost Spire | 6 | 949 | 5 | 6.1 s | New. One straight line laid 60 studs west of the Sisters. |
| **Lantern Line** | North of the Two Sisters to Lantern Key | 3 | 456 | 0 | 3.0 s | Was a dogleg from the temple's river. Now branches off the Frost Road. |
| **Tangle Lane** | West of the Crossroads to Tangle Isle's dock | 5 | 753 | 4 | 4.9 s | Was a hook round Tangle's south-east. Straight. |
| **Leviathan Road** | Between Tangle Isle and the temple, past the Old Man, toward Leviathan's Rest | 5 | 626 | 4 | 4.1 s | New. Stops 300 studs short of the dock on purpose (see below). |
| **Northern Drift** | Frost Spire to Leviathan's Rest along the top of the map | 5 | 740 | 0 | 4.5 s with the current, 5.2 against | Was timed. It is the way across the top, so it is a lane. The Drift Jump is still beside it. |
| **Tide Run** | West of Gull Rock to the edge of the Western Shelf | 4 | 553 | 0 | 3.6 s | New. Then 12 coins show the channel across the shelf to the Tide Vault's pier. |

Removed: the **Back Door Arc** (a loop round an island is not a way to anywhere; its four coins up the Back Door cove stay), the **Reach Run**, the **Ember Reach** and its Anvil Jump.

Three decisions worth knowing about:

- **The Leviathan Road stops short.** Its first draft ended 50 studs from the Sleeper, which wakes to fast boats. A lane must not carry a boat at 170 studs a second onto an island's threat, so it ends outside the Sleeper's hearing and the last 300 studs are the pilot's to judge.
- **The Tide Run's hoops stop at the shelf.** The way on winds between sandbars with turns of 30 to 50 degrees. Hoops there would throw boats at the bars. Coins mark the channel instead.
- **No lane goes to Fort Barnacle, Skull Rock, Driftwood Key or Maelstrom Rock.** The fort has the Serpent Run past it, the skull has the Cinder Slalom to its mouth, the Maelstrom has its ring. Their water is otherwise empty.

| **Serpent Run** | A sprint down the channel between Tangle Isle and the fort | 5 | 480 | 2.9 s with the current, 3.3 against | 4.0 s | Kept as it was. |
| **Lookout Loop** | A lap round Lookout Stack, in open water west of home | 8 | 2058 | 13.3 to 13.8 s a lap | 16 s | New. Replaces the Bay Circuit, out of the harbor's view. Radius 330: the widest turn in the sea. |
| **Maelstrom Ring** | A lap round the outside of the whirlpool | 8 | 1808 | 11.5 to 11.7 s a flying lap | 13.5 s | V5's untimed "Maelstrom Sling" at radius 195 became a timed lap at radius 290. Four big coins are inside it. |

Removed as timed courses: the **Bay Circuit** (replaced), **Pilgrim's Run** and the **Northern Drift** (both lanes now).

**How par was set.** The autopilot drove each course at full chain. Par is its clean time plus 15 to 20 percent, rounded to half a second. A boat that arrives slowly, or misses hoops, will not beat it; one that holds the chain will.

**Laps are new.** A lap starts and ends at its first hoop (the one with the sign), goes either way round, and wants the other seven hoops in order. The clock keeps running, so every lap after the first is a flying lap. Crossing the line again with hoops missed voids that lap and starts a new one. `Coins.lua` holds the logic.

**Rewards are unchanged:** 6 coins for finishing a course once a raid, 10 more the first time under par, the best time and name on the sign.

## 7. Collectibles and reward balance

- **Rates are unchanged.** Ten coins are 1 gold at the Hoard, at most 6 gold a raid. A coin takes half a second off the boost cooldown and patches 1.5 hull. A taken coin comes back after 80 seconds.
- **There is much less to farm.** All the coins in the sea are worth 240, four times one goblin's cap (V5: seven times). Everything within reach of home without leaving the bay is worth 21: the harbor jump, the two passes, the Back Door and Smuggler's lagoon.
- **Coins are now mostly earned.** 27 of the 132 are the big ones, and every big one asks for something: a stack to scrape past, the middle of a jump, the inside of the whirlpool, the fort's harbor.
- **Salvage** is the same crate (8 coins, a keg, 60 hull, a boost refill; four adrift a raid). It is now set adrift 45 to 70 studs to one side of a lane, in deep water: in sight of a boat on the lane, never on its line, and never beside the Gate Run or the Shelf Hop.

I did not change the cap, the rates or any treasure value. With a third of the coins, the cap is harder to reach than it was. Whether coins still feel worth taking is a question for the playtest.

## 8. The view from spawn, and signs

- From the harbor ramp a goblin now sees the water, the reef, the Gate's two posts with one line of hoops through them, the harbor jump's three coins, and the Crossroads beyond. The pictures in section 1 are the same camera in both versions.
- **Signs.** A floating sign has a maximum distance. Roblox measures it along the camera's line of sight, not to the sign, so anything far off to one side still showed. From the harbor a dozen island names stood on the horizon, most of them islands 1,800 studs away or more. The client now hides any sign that is really out of range (`Main.client.lua`; the server tags the signs). At the Hoard that leaves the four near islands, the Crossroads and Windmill Hills.
- "THE GATE" sits lower, between its posts, so it no longer covers the Crossroads' name. The Gate Run has no lane signs, because those two names already stand on its line.
- **Not changed:** treasure tags still show across the map, by design.

![Home Bay in V5](2026-10-12-v6-bay-before.png)

![Home Bay in V6](2026-10-12-v6-bay-after.png)

## 9. The distant explosions

### The source

`Effects.bolt` in the client, unchanged since V2. For every lightning strike it played the boom sound:

- **as an interface sound**, with no position, so it could not fade with distance or come from a direction;
- **at a volume that never went below 0.15**, however far away the strike was;
- **on every client**, because the server sent every strike to everyone.

With three storms out (the usual number since V4) that is a boom every 1.2 seconds, for everyone, all raid. On V2 and V3's smaller maps the storms were closer, and the same formula gives 0.3 to 0.9 within 1,000 studs.

Two smaller faults in the same code:

- **World sounds never faded out.** They used Roblox's default rolloff, which gets quieter with distance but never reaches silence and then cuts off dead at the maximum distance.
- **Each strike made three sounds** (the marker's blip, an explosion boom, and the thunder), and every client built all of it, with the bolt and the marker's parts, for strikes thousands of studs away.

### What changed

| | V5 | V6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thunder | Interface sound. Volume `clamp(1 - distance / 1500, 0.15, 0.9)`. | A world sound at the strike. Full volume within 150 studs, silent at 900, not played at all beyond. Muffled with distance (an equalizer takes up to 30 dB off the treble). Still arrives late, by distance. |
| Every world sound | Default rolloff (`Inverse`), full volume within 15 studs, cut off at its range | `InverseTapered`: the same loudness close by, fading to silence at its range. Not played at all beyond it, or when it would be inaudible. |
| A blast (keg, shell, cannonball) | Full within 15, cut off at 350 | Full within 20, silent at 600 |
| Lightning's explosion boom | Played as well as the thunder | Not played: the thunder is its sound |
| Many blasts at once | All played | At most 3 of one sound within 0.3 s, unless a new one is louder than those. A compressor on the world's sound group (threshold -14 dB, ratio 6) holds down what does overlap. |
| Who is sent a strike | Everyone | Goblins within 1,200 studs (2,000 for the bolt itself). `Net.broadcastNear`, used by `Blast.lua`. |
| What a client draws | Everything | A danger marker or a blast within 900 studs, a bolt within 1,800 |
| The sky's flash | Full, for every strike anywhere | Full within 300 studs, fading to nothing at 1,400 |

Numbers are in `Config.AUDIO`. Nothing about storms, lightning, the Navy or any damage changed.

**Also fixed:** the sky's flash restored whatever colour it found, so two bolts within a tenth of a second could leave the world brightly lit for good.

How loud, by the falloff formula (1 is full volume):

| Distance from the strike | Thunder, V5 | Thunder, V6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 150 studs | 0.90, in your ears | 1.00, from the strike |
| 250 | 0.83 | 0.45 |
| 350 | 0.77 | 0.23 |
| 500 | 0.67 | 0.09 |
| 650 | 0.57 | 0.03 |
| 800 | 0.47 | not played |
| 1,300 and beyond | 0.15, for ever | not played |

### What I measured

I cannot hear. A logger on the client recorded every sound the game created: which file, interface or world, its settings, and how far it was from the camera.

**Before (V5 build).** Standing at the Hoard, three storms 1,600 to 2,900 studs away, 38 seconds:

- 31 thunder sounds, every one an interface sound at volume 0.15.
- 31 marker blips and 31 explosion booms were also created, 1,600 to 2,900 studs away. They were beyond their ranges and inaudible, but every client built them.

**After (V6 build).** Same place, 38 seconds, with three storms set 2,400 to 3,000 studs away and one that drifted past 230 to 750 studs from the Hoard on its own:

- No interface sounds.
- 11 thunder sounds, all from the storm that was near, each at its strike, with loudness by the formula from 0.01 (745 studs) to 0.51 (233 studs) and the treble cut by 7 to 30 dB.
- Nothing from the three far storms. The client was not sent their strikes: it received 11 bolts in that time, the near storm's.

**Inside a storm.** A strike on the goblin: the marker's blip, then thunder at full volume 1.3 seconds later, and no second boom. A strike 234 studs away: 0.5.

**A pile-up.** Six blasts at once, 51 studs away: three booms were played.

**Blasts by distance** (logged with the first setting, full within 15 and silent at 350): played at 36, 71, 131 and 211 studs (0.29, 0.12, 0.04, 0.01), not played at 311 or 411, and one 1,500 studs away was never sent. I then let blasts carry to 600 studs so that one 300 studs off is still faintly heard, and **did not log that final setting.**

### What I cannot say

Whether it sounds right. The loudness figures are the formula, not a measurement of what comes out of the speakers. A person needs to stand in a storm, near one, and at home, and listen.

## 10. Performance

Same machine as the earlier reports. V6 adds no simulation: a lap check in the run timer, a distance check when a blast is sent, and a sign check on the client every 0.4 seconds.

| | V5 | V6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up to world ready | 5.7 to 6.8 s | 5.6 to 6.6 s |
| Generated parts | 5,677 | 5,382 |
| Instances | 52,397 | 52,138 |
| Server, a goblin sailing | 60.0 fps, 0.8 to 0.85 ms of script a frame | 60.0 fps, 0.64 to 0.98 ms, no frame over 20 ms in 6 s |

**Client frame rate, measured for the first time since V2.** Studio's window was in front this time, so the client was not capped.

- At the Crossroads' south dock: **60.0 fps, worst frame 18 ms, no frame over 20 ms in 5 seconds**, with 6,756 instances of the world streamed in (V5's reading there was about 7,500).
- At the Lookout Loop: 60.0 fps, worst frame 18 ms, 6,686 instances.

That is one client on a desktop with nothing happening near it. It says nothing about a phone, a busy scene or four players.

**Not measured in V6:** the demanding scene from the V5 report (FRENZY, two patrol ships, a storm, every creature awake), and memory.

## 11. How it was designed and tested

Worth recording, because it is why this layout is not just another formula.

1. **A survey.** A test command raycast the whole sea on a 10-stud grid (223,000 rays, 1.9 seconds) and classed each cell: land, too shallow for a skiff, skiff and cutter only, deep.
2. **A map.** A small script drew that survey with every hoop, coin, boat, dock, rock and current over it. The before and after pictures in this report are its output, drawn from the running game.
3. **A drawing board.** The same curve maths as `Searuns.lua`, in a script, so a layout could be drawn and checked against the survey (every hoop, every coin, and the water between each pair of hoops) in a second, without starting the game.
4. **The game.** Each layout was built in Studio and the two were compared: all 101 gates and 132 coins within 2.8 studs of the drawing.
5. **An autopilot.** A test command seats the goblin in a skiff and has the server drive it through a lane's hoops with the game's own boat physics: full throttle, steering at a point a little ahead along the course, boosting on the straights, drifting when a turn is sharp. It reports the time, the top speed, the chain, hull lost, and how far it passed from each hoop.
6. **Change, and drive again.** Four layouts were built. Section 13 lists what the driving found.

None of those tools is in the repository (they need a temporary test script and a loopback helper, as in earlier versions). `docs/AI_CONTEXT.md` describes the method.

## 12. Tests performed, and their limits

### Limits that apply to everything below

- **Nobody has played V6.** I can say a boat can follow these lanes. I cannot say they are fun.
- **An autopilot is not a person.** It holds the throttle down and never gets bored, lost or surprised. It is a fair test of "can this be followed at speed" and no test at all of "is this clear" or "is this enjoyable".
- **One AI, one client.** Nothing between two players was exercised.
- **I cannot hear.** Section 9.
- No mobile, gamepad, touch or real-latency test.

### Verified working

- **The world** built with an empty console on each of about ten runs. The machine checks passed on the final build: every treasure spot on its island, all 43 boats over at least 3.2 studs of water, all 11 ziplines clear, no coin on land, no hoop over water too shallow for a skiff.
- **Every lane, both ways** (the table in section 5): every hoop passed within 11 studs, no hull lost, chains of 2 to 6.
- **Every timed course** (the table in section 6): finished, recorded by the game, best time and name written on the sign, coins paid (28 for a first run of the Teeth under par, with the coins along it).
- **Laps:** both rings completed clean laps in both directions and the game recorded them (Maelstrom 11.5 s, Lookout 13.4 s). A chain of 20 hoops was held round the Maelstrom Ring.
- **A goblin's own hands on the wheel:** with the driver's own client simulating the boat and the W key held, the skiff took the Gate Run at 156 studs a second and the HUD showed "HOOP CHAIN x2" (picture below). Nothing was steered.
- **Coins and the purse:** coins collected at 170 studs a second on every lane that has them; 10 coins became 1 gold at the Hoard.
- **A theft and an escape:** took the Lighthouse Lens (Heat +16; the four Watchers left their plinths), raised Heat to HUNTED, and drove the Ember Road as a carrier: 8.1 seconds against 7.9 empty, a chain of 6, with a patrol ship called out and 746 studs behind at the end. Then banked it: 7 gold with interest.
- **A raid ending and starting again:** every coin back, the purse empty, four crates adrift beside lanes, Heat and storms cleared, creatures home.
- **Creatures:** all 21 registered, and one awake with a goblin at home, as in V5.
- **Sound:** section 9.
- **Signs:** read once, just before the goblin spawned (the camera was still 500 studs below the island): 5 island names shown, 17 hidden, and every far sea sign hidden. From the Hoard itself Windmill Hills is in range too, by its distance. The harbor picture in section 1 shows the result: three signs where there were nine.

![Driving the Gate Run: one hoop ahead, in the Gate](2026-10-12-v6-gate-run.jpg)

### Not verified

- **Whether any of it is clearer or more fun to a person.**
- **Anything with two players.**
- **Any ramp.** The harbor jump, the West Jump, the Drift Jump and the Sandbar Jump were not flown in V6. Three of them did not move; the Sandbar Jump's approach is as V5 tested it.
- **The coin trail across the shelf** to the Tide Vault's pier. It was checked against the survey, not driven.
- **Laps by hand.** The autopilot's laps were not all clean: on the Lookout Loop about two in five were, the rest missed a hoop by 20 to 40 studs at full chain. A lap is meant to take some care, but whether 330 studs of radius is forgiving enough for "the one to learn on" is a guess.
- **The escape** used a test command to raise Heat, and I teleported to the Hoard to bank. The patrol ship never caught up, so nothing about being shot at on a lane was seen.
- **The final blast range** by log, and **every sound by ear.**
- **The demanding scene** for performance.
- **The creatures**, beyond the Watchers waking. V6 did not touch them.
- V5's unverified list still stands.

## 13. Bugs found and fixed

In V5's code:

1. **Thunder played to everyone, everywhere, in their ears.** Section 9.
2. **World sounds cut off instead of fading out.**
3. **Two bolts close together could leave the sky lit.**
4. **The Teeth could not be threaded at speed**, and **the Cinder Slalom had a stack on its line.** Section 6.
5. **Salvage crates were dropped onto coins.**
6. **Signs showed from far beyond their range.** Section 8.

In my own V6 drafts, found by driving them:

7. **Laps at radius 190 could not be held.** The autopilot missed half the hoops. 290 can be held; the learner's lap is 330.
8. **The first Tide Run** put hoops through the bends between sandbars.
9. **The first Leviathan Road** ended on top of the Sleeper.
10. **The first Lantern Line** started directly behind the Two Sisters as seen from the Frost Road. A boat turning onto it drove into the rock.
11. **The Frost Road, the first Leviathan Road and the Gate Run had kinks** of 17 to 19 degrees that threw a boat 20 to 120 studs wide of the next hoop. All three are straight lines now.
12. **A wrong property name** in the new sound code stopped the client loading on the first run.
13. **A missed hoop made a lap last two laps** (the clock ran until the hoop was finally taken). Crossing the line now starts a new lap.

Found by Ninety playing V6, after this report was first written:

14. **The Skull Chalice could not be reached.** The ladder shaft from the lagoon to the chamber had rock left across it (it was cut as a round hole 4.5 studs across, and terrain is made of 4-stud cells), and the chamber's floor and throne were laid over the top of the ladder. The geometry dates from V2; every test since had teleported to the chalice, so nobody noticed. The shaft is now cut square and wide and the ladder comes up through a hatch in the floor. Tested on foot: from the pier, up the ladder, onto the landing, round the hatch, and the chalice taken by holding E.
15. **Not fixed, and flagged by the same check:** a scan of all 24 ladders for something over the climber's head found two more that come up under a floor on every side: the windmill's ladder to its gallery (the Golden Gear; the gallery can still be reached by grapple) and the ladder to the fort's cannon stand. Three others (two on the wreck, one in the Crossroads' undercroft) are open on one side and probably fine. None of the five was climbed.

## 14. Remaining limitations

- **Everything in "Not verified".**
- **One coin between hoops on six lanes** may read as too few to mean anything. It is there to top up the boost on a long haul.
- **The lane signs** ("TO EMBER ISLE") are new and unjudged.
- **A sign at the very edge of its range** can blink as the check runs every 0.4 seconds.
- **The two rings are large** (580 and 660 studs across) and sit in open water. They are the biggest single things on the map.
- **The harbor jump's three coins** are the brightest thing in the harbor view. That is deliberate (jump, hoop, Gate) but it is bright.
- **The creatures, treasure values, Heat and the Navy are as V5 left them**, with V5's known issues.
- **The map's regions and the "THE LONG REACH" label** are unchanged.

## 15. Human playtest instructions

Run **Test > Server & Clients > 4 players > Play** if you can. Press `H` first.

**The first minute:**

1. **Stand on the harbor ramp and look out.** Can you tell where to go? Is anything still in the way?
2. **Take the harbor jump and the Gate Run.** Does the line read: jump, hoop, Gate, Crossroads?

**Lanes:**

3. **From the Crossroads' north dock, take the Ember Road.** It is the long one. Can you hold the chain to the end? Is it too easy, too empty, about right?
4. **Go west:** the West Run to the Shoals, or the Tide Run and then follow the coins across the shelf. Could you follow the coins without hitting a sandbar?
5. **Go east:** the Mill Run or the Chimney Run. Did either point somewhere you did not expect?
6. **Anywhere:** did a lane ever throw you at something? Did you ever want a lane and not find one?

**Courses:**

7. **The Lookout Loop** (west of home, orange). Do a few laps. Can you hold it? What time against par 16?
8. **The Teeth** (east of the Crossroads). Is going through the stacks that fast exciting, or just a straight line?
9. **Race someone** round the Maelstrom Ring.

**Coins:**

10. **Did you bother with coins?** Which ones? Did you find a trail that led somewhere?

**Sound. This is the part I could not check:**

11. **Stand at home while a storm is far away.** Any booms?
12. **Sail toward a storm.** Do you hear it before you reach it? Does it get louder? Can you tell which way it is?
13. **Sit inside one.** Is the thunder as dramatic as before?
14. **Throw a keg, fire a cannon, watch a patrol ship shell someone from 200 studs off.** Do those still sound right? Too quiet at a distance?

**With others:**

15. **Did you meet each other on the lanes?**
16. **Carry treasure home down a lane with a patrol ship after you.**

**What I most want to know:** whether the harbor view is now clear or now empty; whether straight lanes are better or duller; and whether the explosions are gone.

## 16. Recommended next priorities

1. **Play it**, with the sound up.
2. **Tune by ear**: thunder's range, how far a blast carries.
3. **The laps**: radius, and whether they are worth their size.
4. **Creature polish**, which V6 left alone as asked.
5. **A demanding-scene performance check** now that the client's frame rate can be read.
6. Still open from before: touch controls; two-player behaviour of the Watchers and the Echo.

## Report: 2026-10-12-v5-living-threats-playful-seas.md

# Report: V5, living threats and playful seas

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-10-12 |
| Request | Ninety's "V5 One-Shot: Living Threats & Playful Seas" prompt |
| Agent | Claude Code (Opus 5.5), local session on Ninety's machine with Roblox Studio MCP |
| Branch | `feature/v5-living-threats-playful-seas`, **stacked on** PR #12's branch `feature/v4-living-archipelago` (then #11, #10, #9) |
| Pull request | [#13](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/13), base branch is `feature/v4-living-archipelago` |
| Merge status | **Not merged.** Nothing was merged, including PRs #9 to #12. Needs a human playtest and explicit approval. |

## 1. Summary

The V4 playtest said three things: the sea is too spread out, the boost hoops are the best part of sailing, and the islands need things living on them. V5 answers all three.

- **The sea is pulled in.** 5080 x 4390 studs, 55% of V4's area (V3: 3200 x 2740, V4: 6900 x 5840). The near islands kept their distance; everything else came about 30% closer. Islands kept their V4 size and features.
- **Hoops are a system now.** 110 of them (V4: 19) laid out as 16 named runs: easy chains on the main lanes, slaloms through the stack fields, six timed runs with a best time on the sign. Taking hoops in a row builds a chain that kicks harder.
- **Coins.** 326 along the runs, round the rocks and in the air over ramps, picked up by driving through at any speed. Each one shortens the boost cooldown and patches the hull a little. Ten are worth 1 gold at the Hoard, at most 6 gold a raid.
- **Salvage and stunts.** Crates float where a patrol ship sank or a storm blew out. Seven ramps (V4: four) have coins hanging over them.
- **Something different lives on every big island.** Twenty-one creatures of thirteen kinds, built on one shared framework. Each has one rule a player can learn: statues that only move when nobody faces them, a double that retraces your steps, a crab that owns the sand, a ram that charges in straight lines, an eel that owns the water, imps that steal from the thief, marines who throw you over the wall, and more. Section 8 is the roster.
- **Retuned** for the shorter trips: raids 9 minutes, far treasure 13 to 20 gold, Heat a little faster.

Tested in Studio by one AI on one client. **Nobody has played V5**, and nothing between two players was exercised. Section 13 says exactly what was and was not verified.

## 2. How I read the prompt, and what I left out

- "About half of V4's area": I took that as a starting point, as the prompt said, and laid the islands out by travel time. The result is 55%. The near ring was already 6 to 8 seconds from home and I left it there.
- "Do not give every island the Guardian with a different skin": no new creature chases a carrier across its island swinging at them. Most do no damage. What they threaten is the treasure, the route, or the ground under you.
- "Preserve boat agency": boat counts are unchanged (43). No creature destroys a boat. The eel and the fin shove boats without damage; only the Sleeper can hurt a hull, it is announced, and its strikes are 45 hull against a skiff's 160.
- **Not built** (ideas from the prompt I chose to leave):
  - **Target challenges** for cannons. Only the cutter and a few emplacements can shoot, so few players would meet them.
  - **Dolphins or other sea creatures to follow.** I wanted a pod whose wake gives a boost; it did not make the cut.
  - **Dynamic events beyond salvage** (a naval battle to loot, for instance).
  - **A creature for every small island.** Pebble Isle, Gull Rock, Smuggler's Cove, Twin Stacks, the Shallows' Kelp Cay, and the three keys have none. The prompt allowed small islands to stay simple.
- **Changed while building:** the imps moved to the pillars beside the shrine and now react to the theft itself (as first placed, a thief leaving by the zipline never passed one). The Watchers were given the job of carrying treasure back, which I had first planned only for the crab.

## 3. Geography: what moved and what was kept

| | V3 | V4 | V5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sea | 3200 x 2740 | 6900 x 5840 | 5080 x 4390 |
| Area, in millions of square studs | 8.8 | 40.3 | 22.3 |
| Against V4 | 22% | 100% | 55% |

**Kept from V4, unchanged:** every island's size and outlands (headlands, crags, inlets, second docks), the harbor chain, beacons, catapults, ziplines, the three new treasures, the regions and their characters, the horizon silhouettes.

**Moved:** every island except the home ring. Because V4 left island positions as one list (`shared/Archipelago.lua`) and built the old islands with an offset, moving them was a change of numbers.

**Re-laid:** everything in the open sea. V4's reef, shelf, stack fields and currents were written in fixed world coordinates and would all have been in the wrong place. `Seaways.lua` now places each of them from the islands' positions (an offset from an island, or a point between two), so they follow the next time the map moves.

**What changed in character:**

- **The Crossing** is now just outside the Gate. The Crossroads is 10 seconds from home, close enough to be the hub it was meant to be.
- **Western Shallows:** the shelf is smaller (radius 400, was 520) and sits tighter between the Shoals, Kelp Cay and the Tide Vault.
- **Navy Waters:** Tangle Isle and Fort Barnacle are about 290 studs apart at the narrowest. The Serpent Channel is a real strait now.
- **Eastern Reach:** Smuggler's Cove and Windmill Hills are close enough that the water between them is a strait too (the Mill Run goes down it).
- **The Long Reach** between the Crossroads and the temple is 460 studs of water with Pilgrim's Rock in the middle. It is no longer long. The name is still on the map.
- **Lost:** the Home Stream current. With the Crossroads this close to the Gate there was no room for it; a hoop run does its job.

| Frost Spire | 17.4 | 43.8 | 30.4 | 69% |
| Skull Rock | 19.5 | 48.9 | 34.5 | 70% |

**Measured in Studio:** a skiff driven by the server at full throttle from the harbor mouth to the Crossroads' beach, standing start, taking the Gate Run's hoops: **589 studs in 6.3 seconds**, top speed 159. V4's same trip was 1000 studs in 10.0 seconds. From the docks it is about 8 seconds.

## 5. The hoop runs

`src/server/Searuns.lua`. A run is a chain of hoops along a line someone would want to sail anyway, about 120 studs apart, so each kick carries into the next. Lane hoops push whichever way you are going.

| Run | Kind | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bay Circuit** | timed, 10 hoops | A lap of the water inside the reef. The first thing to try. |
| Gate Run | lane | Out of the harbor, through the Gate, to the Crossroads' dock |
| Back Door Arc | lane | Coral Atoll, round the south of home past the Back Door, to Pebble Isle |
| West Run | lane, with a ramp | Gull Pass to the Shipwreck Shoals |
| Mill Run | lane | Smuggler's Gap, round Smuggler's Cove, down the strait to Windmill Hills |
| Reach Run | lane | Pilgrim's Rock to Twin Stacks, north of the Teeth |
| Tangle Lane | lane | The temple's south-west shore to Tangle Isle |
| Ember Reach | lane, with a ramp | Crystal Isle's beach, past the Anvil, to Ember Isle |
| Lantern Line | lane | The mouth of the temple's river, past Two Sisters, to Lantern Key |
| Maelstrom Sling | lane | Round the outside of the whirlpool |
| **Pilgrim's Run** | timed, 7 hoops | The Crossroads' north dock, past Pilgrim's Rock, to the temple |
| **The Teeth** | timed slalom, 7 hoops | Between the sea stacks east of the Crossroads. One hoop per gap; the coins weave. |
| **Serpent Run** | timed, 5 hoops | Down the Serpent Channel with the current |
| **Cinder Slalom** | timed slalom, 5 hoops | Through the basalt stacks toward Ember Isle |
| **Northern Drift** | timed, 7 hoops, with a ramp | Along the top of the map with the current |
| Shelf Hop | stunt | Two hoops, the Sandbar Jump, one hoop |

Plus the two hoops at Leviathan's rib run and the three in Coral Atoll's lagoon from before.

**Chains.** A hoop taken within 4 seconds of the last one kicks 5 studs/s harder, up to four steps (30, 35, 40, 45, 50). The boat panel shows "HOOP CHAIN x3" and the note of the sound climbs. A kick never takes a boat past a ceiling (its boosted top speed plus 6 per link: 151 to 175 for a skiff). I added the ceiling after the first test: five hoops and the Serpent's current reached **257 studs/s**, which is unreadable and above what the server's anti-cheat check allows.

**They are offers, not fences.** Nothing blocks the water beside a run. A lane run goes where the lane already went.

## 6. Coins and what they are worth

`src/server/Coins.lua`.

- **Picking up:** pass within 13 studs in a boat (7 on foot). No button. The server checks where hulls and goblins actually are, 20 times a second, and also half way back to the last check so nothing is skipped at speed. The client hides a coin a moment early so it feels instant; it never claims one.
- **Where:** three between each pair of hoops on a run; bigger coins (worth 5) hugging the stacks in the slaloms, deeper in the whirlpool, on the reef's crest and in the fort's harbor; coins in the air over every ramp; and trails that lead into the Back Door, Smuggler's lagoon, the temple's river, Tangle's hidden river, the skull's mouth and under Leviathan's ribs.
- **What a coin does right now:** half a second off the boat's boost cooldown and 1.5 hull patched. A trail of coins keeps a boat boosting and afloat, which is the real reason to take one.
- **What coins are worth:** ten make 1 gold when you are next at the Hoard. **At most 6 gold a raid**, about one middle treasure. The HUD shows the purse and how much has been paid.
- **Against farming:** the cap; a taken coin comes back after 80 seconds; a timed run pays once a raid; everything resets with the raid. There is no second currency and nothing to spend coins on.

All 326 coins together are worth 426, so one goblin sweeping the entire sea would hit the cap about seven times over. The cap is what keeps treasure the score.

## 7. Runs, ramps and salvage

- **Timed runs** start when a boat passes the hoop at either end and finish at the other, hoops in order. Finishing pays 6 coins once a raid, and 10 more the first time it is done under par. The best time stays on the signs at both ends, with a name, for the rest of the session. Wander off and the run is quietly forgotten.
- **Pars are guesses.** They come from the run's length at a brisk speed. Nobody has driven them by hand. A straight server-driven skiff did the Serpent Run in 3.0 seconds against a par of 4.
- **Ramps:** the harbor jump, Coral's kicker, the Sandbar Jump and the Tide Vault's ramp from before, plus the West Jump, the Anvil Jump and the Drift Jump beside three of the lanes. Each has three coins over the flight, the middle one worth 5.
- **Salvage:** a floating crate with a glow and a label. 8 coins, a powder keg, 60 hull patched and the boost refilled. One appears where a patrol ship sinks, one where a storm blows itself out, and four are set adrift on the runs each raid. 150 seconds each, eight at most.

## 8. The inhabitants

`src/server/Creatures.lua` is the shared machinery; `Bestiary.lua` and `BestiaryMinor.lua` are the creatures; the numbers are in `Config.CREATURES`.

| Island | Who | The rule to learn | What it does to you | What you can do about it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Sun Temple** | The Stone Guardian (unchanged from V3) | It pursues carriers; jump the ring | Damage, knocks treasure loose | Outrun it, jump the stomp, leave the island |
| **Crossroads Ruins** | **The Watchers** (4 statues) | They move only while nobody is facing them. Lit eyes mean free to move. | No damage. A touch knocks treasure loose, and a Watcher carries it back to its place. | Face them. Have a friend watch your back. Grab the treasure out of its arms. Sprint: a Watcher does 30 studs/s, which beats a Lens carrier who only runs (25.5) and loses to one who sprints (32). |
| **Crystal Isle** | **The Echo** | A crystal double walks your exact path, 3 seconds behind | 16 damage and treasure loose to whoever it walks into, including a rival on your heels | Never double back. Never stop. Jump over it in the tunnel after the cave-in. |
| **Shipwreck Shoals** | **Old Clacker**, a crab | It travels under sand and shallows. Decks, rock and deep water are not its ground. | A ring warns for 0.85 s, then it comes up: tossed, 10 damage, treasure loose. It reburies treasure left on the sand. | Stay off the sand. Bait it and dash out of the ring. It sits exposed for 4 s afterwards. |
| **Windmill Hills** | **Bramble**, a ram | It charges in a straight line and cannot turn | Tossed a long way, 6 damage. It charges anyone, carrying or not. | Sidestep. Bait it into a cliff (it is dazed). Stand so the toss sends you where you want to go. |
| **Tide Vault** | **The Warden**, an eel | It owns the water. It circles the shallows; after the pearl is taken it hunts whoever is in the water for 30 s. | 12 damage, treasure loose, only in the water | Time its circuit on the way in. On the way out stay on stone: the platform, the columns, the pavilion (grapple between them), or bring the boat to the ramp first. |
| **Tangle Isle** | **The Imps** (2) | A shriek and a marked ring: one is jumping for your treasure and lands in 1.1 s | It takes the treasure and runs across the canopy to a nest in the west | Get off the ring. Or chase it: get close and it drops the treasure and bolts. Left alone for 18 s it puts the treasure back. |
| **Fort Barnacle** | **The Garrison** (2 marines) | The lines on the ground are what a marine can see. Out of the light, you are not there. | A whistle, a charge, and it throws you over the wall. No damage. Treasure stays in the yard. | Stay out of the cone, keep to the walls and roofs (they cannot climb), or use the throw as a way out. |
| **Ember Isle** | **Cinderlings** (3) | They run to where a carrier is going and set fire to it. They never touch you. | Fire on the ground: 8 damage per half second standing in it | Change direction. Stand in the sea and one that follows goes out. |
| **Frost Spire** | **The Chill** | A drifting cold that follows climbers | No damage. Inside it stamina leaks away (6 a second) and none comes back. | Stay ahead of it (it is slower than a run). It attacks the thing you climb with. |
| **Leviathan's Rest** | **The Sleeper** | An eye under the water off the east dock that wakes to the noise of fast boats | Three marked tentacle strikes at the loudest boat (45 hull each) | Slower than 45 makes no noise. Or go fast and straight: the strikes land behind you. |
| **Skull Rock** | **The Captain's shade** | The skull's eyes are lit while he is awake (16 s) and dark while he dozes (9 s). They can be read from the sea. | Nothing by himself | Take the Chalice while the eyes are dark and the ghost fleet is 18 s late |
| **Maelstrom Rock** | **The Maw**, a fin | It circles the whirlpool | Shoves boats along its path. No damage. | Avoid it, or let it push you |
| **Coral Atoll** | **The Clam** | Open 5 s, shut 3 s | Shut on your hand: tossed, 8 damage. The pearl can only be taken while it is open. | Time it |
| **Goblin Cove** | **Gobbo** the dockhand | Friendly | Hands out a powder keg (E), and shouts in the feed when a patrol ship or a storm is near home | |

A blast (a powder keg) stops every creature that can be stopped: Watchers topple for 8 s, the Echo shatters, the crab retreats for 20 s, the ram and the marines are dazed, the eel is stunned, an imp drops what it holds, a cinderling goes out, the Chill scatters.

### How each differs from the Guardian, in one line

The Guardian asks "can you outrun me?" The others ask different questions: *which way are you facing?* (Watchers), *where have you been?* (Echo), *what are you standing on?* (crab, eel), *where will you be in a second?* (ram, imps, cinderlings), *who can see you?* (marines), *how much stamina do you have left?* (the Chill), *how fast are you going?* (the Sleeper), *when do you act?* (the Captain, the clam).

## 9. How they use the world that was already there

- **The Echo and the cave-in.** Taking the Crystal Heart already seals half the tunnel. Now the thief has to turn round in a tunnel with their own double coming up it.
- **The Warden and the flood.** Taking the pearl already slams the gate and floods the vault; the way out is the drain tunnel into the shallows, which is now where the eel hunts. The colonnade and pavilion that were scenery are the safe route.
- **The Imps and the quake.** Taking the Jade Frog already snaps the canopy bridges. An imp that gets the Frog crosses the broken canopy in five seconds; a goblin chasing it has to grapple from pillar to pillar.
- **The Captain and the ghost fleet.** His sleep changes when the existing trouble starts.
- **The Garrison and the fort.** The walls, towers and barracks roofs that were set dressing are now cover and high ground. The catapult from Siege Hill lands a goblin on a barracks roof, above the marines' sight.
- **Old Clacker and the wreck.** The decks and rope bridges are safe ground for a reason now.
- **Rivals.** An Echo hurts whoever walks into it. A Watcher frozen by one goblin's gaze is not chasing another. Bramble tosses anyone. A marine throws out whoever it sees first. None of this was exercised with two players.
- **Treasure that creatures carry stays "loose"** the whole time, so anyone can grab it out of a Watcher's arms or off an imp's nest, and the existing rules (bounds, the Hoard, the grapple) keep working.

## 10. Agency

What I held to, from section 10 of the prompt:

- **No stuns.** Nothing takes control away. The longest loss of control is a toss.
- **No instant kills.** The hardest single hit from a new creature is the Echo's 16. The Sleeper's 24 is a marked area strike.
- **Everything warns.** A ring on the ground (crab, ram, imps, Sleeper), lit eyes (Watchers), lines on the ground (marines), a body you can see coming (eel, fin, Chill, cinderlings), eyes readable from the sea (the Captain).
- **Nothing outruns everything.** The Watchers (30) lose to a sprint and stop for a look. The eel (40) only works in water. The ram (72) cannot turn. The imp can be dodged in 1.1 s.
- **Nothing punishes simply being there**, with two deliberate exceptions: the eel's circuit and Bramble. Both are visible from a long way off, both do little damage, and both are things to play with. If the playtest finds them annoying, making them carrier-only is one condition each.
- **No creature leaves its island.**
- **Boats:** the eel and the fin shove without damage. The Sleeper is the only one that can hurt a hull.

## 11. Treasure, Heat and the economy

| | V4 | V5 | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raid length | 600 s | 540 s | The farthest round trip is a little over two minutes |
| Heat per second carrying | 0.48 | 0.62 | Trips are 30% shorter; the same treasure should end its trip at about the same Heat |
| Fort's waters | 1500 | 1150 | Scaled with the sea |
| Beacon range | 1500 | 1100 | Scaled with the sea |
| Storms seeded from a player | 700 to 1300 | 600 to 1050 | Scaled with the sea |
| Treasure | 1 to 24 | 1 to 20 | See below |

New values, in gold: Captain's Chest 5, Crystal Heart 7, Pearl of the Deep and Tempest Trident 8, Jade Frog, Storm Lantern and Castaway's Hoard 9, Admiral's Strongbox and Ember Crown 13, Golden Idol 14, Aurora Gem and Leviathan Tooth 17, Skull Chalice 20. The cheaper ones are unchanged.

Values came down less than distances did (about 15% against 30%), because every big island is now harder to leave with its treasure. That is a judgment, not a measurement. **The one I am least sure of:** treasures whose island creature takes the treasure back (Lens, Chest, Frog) may now be worth too little for the trouble, and the three keys' treasures (9 gold, no creature) may be the best deal on the map.

Coins add at most 6 gold a raid per goblin. Boats: unchanged.

## 12. Architecture and performance decisions

- **One creature framework, small behaviors.** `Creatures.lua` gives every creature a body (one anchored root, the rest welded, so moving it is one write), sleep, ground and water queries, walking that follows the ground, player lookups, one way to hurt or shove a player, one way to mark a spot, and the reset, treasure-taken and blast hooks. A creature is a table with `build`, `tick`, `reset`. The seven in `Bestiary.lua` are about 160 lines each, the seven in `BestiaryMinor.lua` about 95.
- **Sleep.** A creature is only ticked while a player is within its wake range of its home, or while it is in the middle of something. With one player at home, 1 of 21 is active.
- **Kinematic, like the Guardian.** Creatures never collide, so they cannot shove treasure off the map or wedge a boat. They answer no raycasts, so a grapple aimed at one goes to the ground behind it.
- **Treasure in a creature's grip** is three small functions in `Loot.lua` (`hold`, `letGo`, `sendHome`) that keep the item in its ordinary "loose" state. I did not add a new state to the treasure state machine.
- **Coins are server parts.** 326 of them. The alternative, drawing them on each client from a list, would save instances and cost a second code path; streaming already keeps a client from holding ones it cannot see.
- **Hoops are eight bars, not sixteen cubes**, because there are a hundred of them.
- **The sea is placed from island positions**, so the next change of layout is a change of numbers.
- **The server decides** every pickup, every run time, every purse payment and everything a creature does. Clients send nothing new: no remote was added.
- **Start-up** is a little quicker than V4 because the sea is smaller.

### Measurements

Same machine and method as the V4 report.

| | V3 | V4 | V5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up to world ready | 2.9 s | 6.4 to 7.5 s | 5.7 to 6.8 s |
| Generated parts | 2,333 | 4,742 | 5,677 |
| Instances | 48,236 | 51,295 | 52,397 |
| Sea-depth cells | 5,520 | 25,258 | 13,970 |
| Boats | 14 | 43 | 43 |
| Server, idle | 60.0 fps, 0.8 to 0.9 ms of script a frame | 60.0, 0.05 to 0.9 | 60.0, 0.8 to 0.85 |

- **Every creature ticking at once** (forced, as if a goblin stood on every island): 0.99 ms of script a frame against 0.85 with one awake. 60.0 fps.
- **A demanding scene:** FRENZY Heat, two patrol ships chasing, a storm overhead, all 21 creatures ticking, 4 salvage crates. Over 6 seconds: **59.2 fps mean, 8 frames over 20 ms, worst frame 56 ms**, 1.21 ms of script a frame. The spike is at the moment the ships are created.
- **The game's script memory:** 6 to 7 MB.
- **Client frame rate: not measured.** Studio's window was in the background again, which caps the client at 15 fps (measured: 15.0).
- **A thing to watch on weaker devices:** with the islands closer, more of the world sits inside the streaming radius. A client standing at the Crossroads held about 7,500 instances of the world. I did not take the same reading in V4, so I cannot say how much more that is, and I have no frame-rate number to go with it.

## 13. Tests performed, and their limits

### Limits that apply to everything below

- **Nobody has played V5.** I can say things work as written, not that they are fun or fair.
- **One AI, one client.** Nothing between two players was exercised: no Watcher held by one goblin while it chased another, no Echo hurting a rival, no coin taken by two boats at once.
- The client ran at 15 fps. Creatures were tested by teleporting a goblin to them and standing still or facing a direction; **no creature has faced a moving, dodging player.**
- No mobile, gamepad, touch or real-latency test.

### Verified working

- **The world** built with an empty console on every run (about fifteen), and after each change of layout the machine checks passed: all 19 treasure spots and the Hoard on their islands, all 43 boats over at least 3.2 studs of water, all 11 ziplines clear, no hoop over land.
- **A full loop:** stole the Lost Compass, banked it (+1 gold), raid end, reset.
- **Hoops:** a server-driven skiff on the Gate Run reached 164 before the ceiling and 159 after; on the Serpent Run 257 before and 177 after. A **client-driven** skiff (the W key held, the driver's own physics) took the Gate Run: the chain showed, coins were collected (45 in the purse), no errors.
- **A timed run:** the Serpent Run started, finished, paid 16 coins and wrote the best time (3.0 s) and the driver's name on its sign.
- **The purse:** 28 coins became 2 gold at the Hoard. **Salvage:** a crate gave coins and a keg. **Reset:** every coin back, purse empty, four crates adrift.
- **The Sandbar Jump** still works at its new place (checked by depth and position, not re-flown after the move).
- **Watchers:** advanced at 30 studs/s with the goblin's back turned, stopped dead when faced, knocked the Lens loose, and another carried it back to the lighthouse in 7 s.
- **Echo:** reached a goblin who stood still 3.0 s after the theft and hit for 16.
- **Old Clacker:** came under the sand, warned, came up, tossed for 10. The first toss did not loosen the Chest (the usual 1.5 s of protection after a grab); the second did, and it reburied the Chest within 8 s.
- **Bramble:** 0.9 s of warning, charged, tossed the goblin about 50 studs into the sea, stopped at the water's edge.
- **The Warden:** shocked a goblin standing on its circuit twice as it passed (11 each). After the pearl was taken it left its circuit, crossed the shallows at 40 studs/s and shocked the thief; the pearl dropped.
- **Imps:** on the theft one leapt in 1.1 s, took the Frog, reached the nest in 5 s across seven perches, and dropped the Frog when the goblin arrived at the nest.
- **Garrison:** a marine saw the goblin in its cone, whistled, and threw them over the south wall into the harbor.
- **Cinderlings:** ran to within 11 studs of a carrier and laid 33 patches of fire in 5 s without touching them; went home when the carrier left.
- **The Chill:** stamina fell at 6 a second inside it.
- **The Sleeper:** awareness rose with a skiff at 104 studs/s, struck at full, and the strikes missed the boat. A boat left circling near it earlier was later found at 54 of 160 hull.
- **The Captain:** with the eyes dark, the Chalice was taken and the ghost ships appeared 18 s later.
- **The Maw** shoved a parked skiff. **The Clam** shut on a goblin and tossed them; opened again after 3 s.
- **A blast on each of nine creatures**: no errors, and each reacted as written.

### Not verified

- **Anything with two players**, as above.
- **Any creature against a player who moves.** In particular whether the Watchers can be outrun, whether the imp's ring can be dodged in 1.1 s, whether Bramble's line can be read, whether the cinderlings actually cut a runner off.
- **Driving the runs by hand**, apart from holding W up the Gate Run. The slaloms, the Bay Circuit and every par are untested.
- **Gobbo's** keg and his warnings. **Bramble's temper** after the Gear is taken. **A cinderling going out in the sea.** **The Captain awake** (the ordinary case: the fleet rises at once, as in V4).
- **Salvage from a sunk patrol ship or a spent storm** (the crate itself was tested; the two events that drop one were not made to happen).
- **A coin coming back after 80 s.** **The 6-gold cap being reached.**
- **Client frame rate.**
- V4's unverified list (walking the new land, riding ziplines, the inlets) is still open, and the islands have moved since.

## 14. Bugs found and fixed while testing

1. **A hoop chain reached 257 studs/s.** Kicks now stop at a ceiling.
2. **A walker never arrived.** A creature closing on its stopping distance crept toward it for ever (floating point), so the first Watcher stood beside the lighthouse holding the Lens and never put it back. One small margin.
3. **The imps never met a thief.** See section 2.
4. **The Chill did nothing.** Stamina came back faster than it leaked.
5. **The Captain's clock stopped when nobody was near**, so the eyes flipped the moment someone arrived. It now runs by the clock.
6. **Bramble charged at swimmers** and stopped at the water's edge, again and again.
7. **Pilgrim's Run went over Pilgrim's Rock's beach and dock.** Re-routed past its west side. (The builder now warns about any hoop over water too shallow for a skiff, and Main prints the warnings.)
8. **A zipline ended in the hill it lands on** after the move. Its end is higher.
9. **A marine's patrol went through the south wall** (a slip in its route numbers).
10. **A text splice doubled the island list** while I was moving the islands. Caught at once; mentioned because the fix was to stop splicing by hand.

## 15. Known issues

- **The pars are guesses**, and so are most creature numbers. Expect to change them after one session.
- **Creatures are kinematic.** They walk through walls and props (a marine goes through a barracks), and a Watcher will climb the outside of the lighthouse to put the Lens back.
- **Creatures are blocky.** They are a few parts each.
- **The coin and hoop count** adds about 900 parts to the world.
- **Old Clacker will not follow treasure into the water**, so a Chest dropped in the lagoon is safe from it.
- **Gobbo stands a little above the ground.**
- **The map's region names** are placed by hand and "THE LONG REACH" no longer describes its water.
- **Floating names on the horizon** stack more than they did in V4, because more of the world is in view.
- Everything in V4's known issues that was not about distance still applies.

## 16. Human playtest instructions

Run **Test > Server & Clients > 4 players > Play** if you can. Press `H` first: the help panel mentions hoops, coins and the islands' inhabitants.

**Alone, ten minutes:**

1. **Sail the Bay Circuit** (orange hoops just outside the harbor). Is chaining hoops fun? Is the top speed still controllable? What time did you get against the par?
2. **Take the Gate Run to the Crossroads.** Is 10 seconds the right distance now? Too close?
3. **Collect coins on the way.** Does picking them up feel instant? Do you care about them? Go home with ten or more and stand on the Hoard.
4. **Try one slalom** (the Teeth, east of the Crossroads). Fair, or do you just hit rocks?
5. **Look for a salvage crate** (a glowing box with a label).

**The islands, one at a time. For each: could you tell what the thing was doing, and did knowing help?**

6. **Crossroads:** take the Lens and come down. Watch the statues. Turn your back, then turn round.
7. **Crystal Isle:** take the Heart and leave through the tunnel. Then try doubling back.
8. **Shipwreck Shoals:** take the Chest and cross the sand. Then try staying on the wreck and the bridges.
9. **Windmill Hills:** walk into the west meadow.
10. **Tide Vault:** wade in, take the pearl, and get out without touching the water.
11. **Tangle Isle:** take the Frog. Dodge the imp, or chase it.
12. **Fort Barnacle:** get to the keep without being seen. Then get seen on purpose.
13. **Ember Isle, Frost Spire:** take the treasure and come down.
14. **Leviathan's Rest:** sail to the east dock slowly, then fast.
15. **Skull Rock:** watch the eyes from the sea before you go in.

**With others:**

16. **Did you meet each other more than in V4?** Where?
17. **Use a creature on a rival.** Lead someone into your Echo. Let a Watcher have someone else's treasure and take it from its arms. Get Bramble to toss them.
18. **Race a timed run** and beat each other's time on the sign.
19. **Frame rate** at the Crossroads, where the most is in view. Say what device.

**What I most want to know:** which creature was the best and which was just annoying; whether any island is now not worth robbing; whether coins matter; and whether the sea is the right size.

## 17. Recommended next priorities

1. **Play it and cut.** Thirteen kinds of creature in one pass will not all be good. Keep the three or four that make people laugh or swear, and spend the next pass making those deeper.
2. **Tune the pars and the creature numbers** from real play.
3. **Two-player behavior** of the Watchers and the Echo, which is where I expect the best stories and have tested nothing.
4. **Check the treasure values** against section 11's worry.
5. **A creature each for the keys**, if the keys turn out to be free money.
6. **Client performance** at the Crossroads on a weak device.
7. Still open from before: touch controls; the insides of the old treasure sites at V3's speeds.

## Report: 2026-10-12-v4-living-archipelago.md

# Report: V4, the living archipelago

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-10-12 |
| Request | Ninety's "V4 One-Shot: The Living Archipelago" prompt |
| Agent | Claude Code (Opus 5.5), local session on Ninety's machine with Roblox Studio MCP |
| Branch | `feature/v4-living-archipelago`, **stacked on** PR #11's branch `feature/v3-speed-agency-danger` (itself stacked on PR #10, then PR #9) |
| Pull request | [#12](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/12), base branch is `feature/v3-speed-agency-danger` |
| Merge status | **Not merged.** Nothing was merged, including PRs #9, #10 and #11. Needs a human playtest and explicit approval. |

## 1. Summary

The V3 playtest said the goblin and the boats now feel right, and that they have outgrown the world: a skiff crossed the whole map in 20 seconds. V4 rebuilds the geography around what the player can now do.

- **The sea is 4.6 times bigger** (6900 x 5840 studs, was 3200 x 2740) and is laid out in **regions** with different characters, not in even rings.
- **Every large island is bigger and has more than one way in**: headlands, hills, cliff-walled crags, hidden inlets a boat can follow, second docks. The treasure sites themselves are unchanged.
- **The water between islands has things in it**: a reef that closes Home Bay, a shelf of shallows only small boats can cross, three fields of sea stacks, a narrow fast strait, lone rocks to steer by, seven currents and sixteen boost hoops.
- **Five new kinds of thing to use**: a harbor chain that locks the Navy in port, signal beacons that send patrol ships the wrong way, catapults, ziplines off the new crags, and boat ramps over sandbars.
- **Four new small islands** as places to stop on the long crossings, three with a small treasure (19 treasures in all).
- **Far islands stay on the horizon** as plain silhouettes that never stream out.
- **Numbers retuned for the distances**: far treasure pays more, Heat builds slower per second, storms are seeded near players, raids are 10 minutes, every island has a boat (43, was 14).

The game is tested in Studio by one AI on one client. **Nobody has played V4.** Start-up takes about 7 seconds (V3: 3). Section 12 says exactly what was and was not verified.

## 2. How I read the prompt, and what I did not do

- "Substantially larger" is tied to travel time, not to a multiplier. I sized the sea so that a near island is 6 to 8 seconds by skiff, a middle island 13 to 29, and a far one 37 to 49. Section 4 has the table.
- "Not uniform scaling": islands were not scaled. The eight original islands were **moved whole** (their terrain lands on the same voxels, so their shapes are identical), and new land was generated around all of them.
- I kept every V3 system and did not change movement, stamina, dash, air jump, grapple, Poltergoblin, drift or boost.
- I did not add progression, shops, new boats, or weapons. The three new treasures use existing models and existing trouble.
- I did not rebuild the inside of any treasure site. Routes inside the Sun Temple, the Fort's keep, the Tide Vault and so on are as they were in V3.
- **Two things in the plan changed while building.** Twin Stacks stayed beside Crystal Isle (the zipline between them is the reason they exist) instead of moving next to the Crossroads; the stack field near the Crossroads is a new feature, the Teeth. And the hook posts I planned as a general tool ended up only at the Gate: sea stacks and crags are already things to grapple.

## 3. The shape of the sea

North is up (-Z). Goblin Cove is in the south.

| Region | Islands | Character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Home Bay** | Goblin Cove, Pebble Isle, Coral Atoll, Gull Rock, Smuggler's Cove | Sheltered. Wrecker's Reef closes the bay to the north with one deep gap (the Gate) and two shallow passes. |
| **The Crossing** | Crossroads Ruins | The hub. Every northern route passes it. The Home Stream runs from it down to the Gate. |
| **Western Shallows** | Shipwreck Shoals, Kelp Cay (new), the Tide Vault | A sandy shelf 4.8 studs deep and about 800 across, with dry bars to steer around. A patrol ship cannot enter it. |
| **Eastern Reach** | Windmill Hills, Crystal Isle, Twin Stacks, Maelstrom Rock | A cluster, then one rock alone in open water. The Teeth (a stack field) lie between it and the Crossroads. |
| **Navy Waters** | Tangle Isle, Fort Barnacle, Driftwood Key (new) | Within 1500 studs of the fort, patrol ships launch from its harbor. The Serpent Channel runs between the two big islands with the fastest current in the sea. |
| **The Far North** | Sun Temple, Pilgrim's Rock (new), Frost Spire, Leviathan's Rest | Long open crossings, with lone rocks (the Old Man, Two Sisters, North Pillar) as the only landmarks. |
| **The Cinders** | Ember Isle, Lantern Key (new), Skull Rock | Basalt stacks scattered between three islands. |

Why these shapes:

- **Remote islands** (Skull Rock, Frost Spire, Leviathan's Rest) are far from everything, so going is a commitment and a lost boat is a real problem. Each now has a spare boat.
- **Clusters** (Home Bay, Eastern Reach, the Cinders) put several goblins in the same water, so they meet.
- **A narrow strait** (the Serpent Channel) and **a gated bay** (Home Bay) are the two places the map forces a choice of line.
- **Sheltered water** (the Shallows) is somewhere a thief in a small boat is safe from the Navy, at the price of a slower, twistier route.
- **Staging points** (the four keys and rocks) break the longest legs. Each has a dock and a skiff; three have a beacon.

The world map (`M`) now shows the region names.

**Keeping the trips busy.** A longer trip is only better if something happens on it.
